## Detailed Directory of the Newly Added 20 Endpoints

The 20 endpoints below provide specialized functionality supporting **Select & Sell** catalog sharing and the modern **Seller Panel V2** standalone merchant workspace. Below is an exhaustive breakdown of each newly introduced endpoint, categorized by functional domain:

### 1. Select & Sell Endpoints (3 Endpoints)

The **MP Select and Sell** feature allows multiple vendors to attach their offers (custom price, inventory, condition) to a single master product in the marketplace catalog, eliminating duplicate catalog listings.

#### 1. Select and Sell (`select-and-sell`)
- **Default Slug**: `select-and-sell`
- **Default Title**: `Select and Sell`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Loads the vendor's Select & Sell management dashboard. Displays a data table of all existing catalog products that the merchant is currently offering. Shows current selling prices, stock levels, product status, and action links to modify terms or view competitor offers.
- **Reference Guide**: [Admin Select and Sell](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/admin-select-and-sell.html) and [Selling Existing Products](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/selling-existing-products.html).

#### 2. Add Select and Sell Product (`add-selected-sell-product`)
- **Default Slug**: `add-selected-sell-product`
- **Default Title**: `Add Select and Sell Product`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Onboarding screen loaded when a vendor chooses an existing catalog item to sell. Allows the seller to configure their specific regular price, sale price, stock quantity, stock status, product condition (New, Used, Refurbished), and upload seller-specific gallery images without re-creating product descriptions or taxonomies.
- **Reference Guide**: [Selling Existing Products](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/selling-existing-products.html).

#### 3. Edit Select and Sell Product (`edit-selected-sell-product`)
- **Default Slug**: `edit-selected-sell-product`
- **Default Title**: `Edit Select and Sell Product`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Dedicated editor interface for existing mapped catalog products. Sellers can update price points, modify available stock inventory, adjust promotional sale dates, or update condition descriptions.
- **Reference Guide**: [Selling Existing Products](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/selling-existing-products.html).

---

### 2. Catalog & Bulk Listing Endpoints (4 Endpoints)

These endpoints provide modern catalog authoring and bulk spreadsheet import tools within the Seller Panel V2.

#### 4. List Your Product (`seller-list-product`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-list-product`
- **Default Title**: `List Your Product`
- **Target Page & Capability**: The modern Seller Panel V2 product authoring workflow. Replaces the legacy product form with an intuitive wizard featuring category search trees, GTIN/EAN/UPC barcode validation, Magic AI automated product copywriting, and instant publication controls.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Product Management](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-product-management.html) and [Generate Product Content](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/generate-product-content.html).

#### 5. Bulk Upload (`seller-bulk-upload`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-bulk-upload`
- **Default Title**: `Bulk Upload`
- **Target Page & Capability**: End-to-end spreadsheet catalog import suite. Vendors can download sample CSV and XLS templates, upload bulk product spreadsheets, map spreadsheet columns to WooCommerce attributes, and execute automated background import jobs with error reporting.
- **Reference Guide**: [Bulk Upload](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/bulk-upload.html).

#### 6. Search Products (`seller-search-products`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-search-products`
- **Default Title**: `Search Products`
- **Target Page & Capability**: High-speed catalog search engine within Seller Panel V2. Allows merchants to search the marketplace catalog by product title, SKU, barcode, or category to quickly locate an existing product and click **Sell Yours** to open the Select & Sell assignment workflow.
- **Reference Guide**: [Selling Existing Products](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/selling-existing-products.html).

#### 7. Sell Catalog Products Bulk (`seller-bulk-sell-products`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-bulk-sell-products`
- **Default Title**: `Sell Catalog Products Bulk`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Batch assignment tool for Select & Sell. Vendors upload a CSV mapping existing product IDs or SKUs with their custom prices and stock quantities, attaching their store to dozens or hundreds of existing catalog items in a single batch operation.
- **Reference Guide**: [Bulk Upload](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/bulk-upload.html) and [Selling Existing Products](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/selling-existing-products.html).

---

### 3. Fast Inventory & Pricing Management Endpoints (4 Endpoints)

High-speed operational endpoints designed to let merchants maintain inventory levels and pricing without navigating into individual product editing pages.

#### 8. Manage Inventory (`seller-manage-inventory`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-manage-inventory`
- **Default Title**: `Manage Inventory`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Dedicated inventory control dashboard with stock status indicators (In Stock, Out of Stock, On Backorder), SKU references, and inline stock quantity editing directly inside the table grid.
- **Reference Guide**: [Manage Inventory](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-inventories.html).

#### 9. Inventory Variations (`seller-manage-inventory-variations`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-manage-inventory-variations`
- **Default Title**: `Inventory Variations`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Granular stock manager for variable products. Expands variable product hierarchies to show every attribute combination (e.g., Size: L, Color: Blue) with individual SKUs and editable stock levels.
- **Reference Guide**: [Manage Inventory](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-inventories.html).

#### 10. Manage Pricing (`seller-manage-pricing`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-manage-pricing`
- **Default Title**: `Manage Pricing`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Dedicated pricing management matrix. Allows merchants to audit regular prices, promotional sale prices, and active discounts across simple and parent products with inline editing and bulk price modification utilities.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Product Management](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-product-management.html).

#### 11. Pricing Variations (`seller-manage-pricing-variations`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-manage-pricing-variations`
- **Default Title**: `Pricing Variations`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Variation-level pricing console. Enables vendors to configure distinct regular prices, sale prices, and scheduled promotional dates for each individual child variation of a variable product.
- **Reference Guide**: [Manage Inventory](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-inventories.html).

---

### 4. Performance, Health & Reviews Endpoints (3 Endpoints)

These endpoints give vendors visibility into customer satisfaction, store quality metrics, and compliance standings.

#### 12. Account Health (`seller-account-health`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-account-health`
- **Default Title**: `Account Health`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Vendor performance scorecard that computes store standing (Healthy, At Risk, Critical). Tracks Order Defect Rate (ODR), Late Dispatch Rate, Cancellation Rate, and policy compliance with visual gauge meters and performance improvement guidance.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Account Health](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-account-health.html).

#### 13. Seller Reviews (`seller-reviews`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-reviews`
- **Default Title**: `Seller Reviews`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Store-level customer feedback directory. Displays multi-criteria ratings (Price, Value, Quality), written customer reviews, buyer details, and date filters, helping merchants evaluate customer sentiment regarding fulfillment and service.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Seller Review](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-seller-review.html).

#### 14. Product Reviews (`seller-product-reviews`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-product-reviews`
- **Default Title**: `Product Reviews`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Product catalog review feed. Aggregates all verified buyer reviews, star ratings, and feedback comments submitted across products owned by the vendor, with search and filtering by product title or rating score.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Product Review](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-product-review.html).

---

### 5. Analytics & Customer Management Endpoints (4 Endpoints)

Comprehensive merchant intelligence endpoints providing deep insights into sales performance, product velocity, and buyer relationships.

#### 15. Sales Reporting (`seller-reporting-sales`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-reporting-sales`
- **Default Title**: `Sales Reporting`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Dynamic sales analytics console with interactive trend graphs and summary KPI cards. Displays gross revenue, net vendor commission, total orders, refund totals, tax amounts, and date filters (today, 7 days, 30 days, year-to-date, or custom period) with CSV and PDF export options.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Sales Reporting](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-sales-reporting.html).

#### 16. Products Reporting (`seller-reporting-products`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-reporting-products`
- **Default Title**: `Products Reporting`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Catalog performance analytics breakdown identifying top-selling items, high-revenue products, units sold, and stock turnover metrics to help vendors optimize their product catalog.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Products Reporting](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-products-reporting.html).

#### 17. Customers Reporting (`seller-reporting-customers`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-reporting-customers`
- **Default Title**: `Customers Reporting`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Customer behavior analytics interface displaying repeat purchase rates, new vs. returning buyer ratios, average buyer lifetime spend, and customer geographic distribution.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Customer Reporting](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-customer-reporting.html).

#### 18. Customers (`seller-customers`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-customers`
- **Default Title**: `Customers`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Direct merchant CRM directory listing all registered buyers who have purchased products from the vendor. Shows customer name, email address, order count, total revenue generated, and direct links to order histories.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Customer List](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-customer-list.html).

---

### 6. Dashboard Personalization & Site Settings Endpoints (2 Endpoints)

Preferences and display configuration screens allowing vendors to tailor the Seller Panel V2 workspace to their operational preferences.

#### 19. Graph Setting (`seller-graph-setting`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-graph-setting`
- **Default Title**: `Graph Setting`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Dashboard chart customization screen. Vendors can select chart types (Line chart, Bar chart, or Spline chart) and customize primary, secondary, and accent color palettes for all visual analytics widgets and reporting graphs.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Graph Setting](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-graph-setting.html).

#### 20. Site Setting (`seller-site-setting`)
- **Default Slug**: `seller-site-setting`
- **Default Title**: `Site Setting`
- **Target Page & Capability**: Seller Panel V2 workflow customization screen. Enables vendors to choose product authoring layouts (Horizontal Tabs, Vertical Tabs, or Stacked Form), toggle the 3-step creation wizard stepper, and track real-time **Listing Completeness** scores.
- **Reference Guide**: [Vendor Site Setting](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-site-setting.html).

---

## Standalone Seller Panel Base Configuration

The **Seller Panel Base** setting is a unique configuration that powers the standalone vendor dashboard:

- **Endpoint (URL Base Slug)**
  - **Default**: `seller`
  - **Purpose**: Defines the first path segment of the dedicated vendor portal (e.g., `https://example.com/seller/`).
  - Instead of loading vendor features inside `/my-account/`, the standalone seller panel serves all vendor endpoints under this independent URL path.
  - **Example**:
    - My Account mode: `https://example.com/my-account/vendor-dashboard/`
    - Standalone mode: `https://example.com/seller/vendor-dashboard/`

- **Title**
  - **Default**: `Seller Panel`
  - **Purpose**: Sets the WordPress page title used by the seller panel page in the WordPress admin page hierarchy. Individual vendor screens still display their own section titles.

::: warning Important Naming Rule
The Seller Panel Base slug must **never** match an existing WooCommerce endpoint slug, WordPress page slug, or category slug. Renaming this field automatically renames the underlying WordPress page that serves the seller panel.
:::

---

## Best Practices for Endpoint Management

To ensure seamless navigation and prevent routing errors on your marketplace, follow these recommendations:

1. **Keep Slugs Lowercase and URL-Friendly**
   - Always use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens (`-`).
   - Avoid uppercase letters, spaces, underscores, or special symbols (e.g., use `vendor-orders` instead of `Vendor_Orders!`).

2. **Ensure Every Slug is Unique**
   - Never duplicate an endpoint slug across two different sections.
   - Ensure endpoint slugs do not clash with standard WooCommerce endpoints (such as `orders`, `downloads`, `edit-account`, or `customer-logout`).

3. **Flush Permalinks After Changes**
   - Whenever you modify an endpoint slug or the Seller Panel Base slug, WordPress rewrite rules must refresh.
   - Navigate to **WordPress Admin > Settings > Permalinks** and click **Save Changes** to prevent 404 "Page Not Found" errors.

4. **Consistent Prefixing**
   - Use a clear prefix like `vendor-` for all vendor-specific endpoints. This ensures zero collisions with native customer account pages or other third-party extensions.

# Configuration – Google Analytics

The **Google Analytics** feature allows the admin and vendors to track website and product performance using Google Analytics (GA-4).

---

## Google Analytics Overview

- Helps analyze customer behavior and store performance
- Tracks product views, purchases, and sales data
- Supports real-time analytics and debug mode

---

## Admin Configuration Path

To configure Google Analytics and Google Map settings for your marketplace:

1. Log in to your **WordPress Admin Panel**.
2. In the left navigation menu, go to **Marketplace > Settings**.
3. Select the **Google Analytics** tab.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/google-analytics-map.webp"><img src="./assets/google-analytics-map.webp" alt="Google Analytics and Map" /></a>

---

## Google Analytics Settings Summary

The table below provides a quick reference for each setting on the Google Analytics settings page:

| Setting Label | Input Type | Default Setting | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Enable Google analytics** | Checkbox | Enabled | Turns on Google Analytics 4 tracking across the entire marketplace. |
| **Measurement ID** | Text Field | `G-XXXXXXXXXX` | Admin Measurement ID used to collect marketplace-wide traffic and sales data. |
| **Allow vendor to use Google Analytics** | Checkbox | Enabled | Allows sellers to connect their own Google Analytics account from their profile. |
| **Enable tracking events** | Checkbox | View Item & Purchase Enabled | Selects which customer interactions (product views and purchases) are tracked. |
| **Enable debug mode** | Checkbox | Enabled | Displays live event activity instantly in Google Analytics DebugView. |
| **Google Map API Key** | Text Field | Optional | Populates geographic sales maps and top billing countries on the vendor dashboard. |

---

## Google Analytics Settings

### Enable Google Analytics

- Enable to populate Google Analytics data on the marketplace

- **Help Tip**: *If checked, google analytics data will be populated.*
- **How It Works**:
  - When checked, the marketplace loads Google Analytics (GA-4) tracking scripts across your storefront pages.
  - Activates site-wide tracking for page visits, customer interactions, and purchases.
  - If unchecked, all analytics tracking scripts remain disabled and no store data is sent to Google Analytics.

---

### Measurement ID

- Enter the Google Analytics **GA-4 Measurement ID**
- Can be obtained from the Google Analytics account
- [Click here to learn how to get the Measurement ID](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/google-analytics.md)

- **Help Tip**: *Google analytics tracking ID to be obtained from Google Analytics Account.*
- **Measurement ID Format**: Google Analytics 4 IDs start with **`G-`** followed by 10 letters or numbers (such as `G-JF7Q9MCL96`).
- **Scope**: Acts as the central tracking ID for the marketplace administrator. All storefront browsing activity, product page visits, and orders are collected in this property.
- For detailed setup steps, see our guide on [How to Get a Google Analytics Measurement ID](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/google-analytics.html).

---

### Allow Vendor to Use Google Analytics

- Enables vendors to connect and use their own GA account
- Vendors can track their individual store performance

- **Help Tip**: *If checked, vendor can also configure Google Analytics for their sales.*
- **How It Works**:
  - When enabled, sellers see dedicated Google Analytics settings inside their **Vendor Profile** page.
  - Each seller can enter their own personal Measurement ID and choose which tracking events to enable.
  - When shoppers browse or purchase products from a specific vendor, data is recorded in both the admin marketplace analytics and the vendor's personal analytics property.

---

### Enable Tracking Events

- Enable required tracking events:
  - View Item Event
  - Purchase Event

You can selectively enable the following e-commerce tracking events:

#### View Item Event
- **Help Tip**: *If checked, view item event will be sent to Google Analytics - 4.*
- **When It Triggers**: Fires automatically when a shopper views a single product page.
- **Tracked Details**:
  - Store Currency and Product Price
  - Product ID and Product Title
  - Product Categories (including parent and child categories)

#### Purchase Event
- **Help Tip**: *If checked, purchase event will be sent to Google Analytics - 4.*
- **When It Triggers**: Fires automatically when a buyer completes checkout and views the **Order Received** (Thank You) confirmation page.
- **Compatibility**: Works seamlessly with standard WooCommerce checkout pages as well as modern block-based checkouts.
- **Tracked Details**:
  - Order Number and Total Order Value
  - Taxes and Shipping Charges
  - Applied Discount Coupons
  - Purchased Items list (Product Name, SKU/ID, Unit Price, Quantity, Brand, and Selected Variations)

---

### Enable Debug Mode

- Enables real-time event tracking
- Allows admin and vendors to:
  - Verify events instantly
  - View data in GA-4 Debug View

- **Help Tip**: *If checked, real time analytics can be seen in analytics account under Admin -> Data Display -> DebugView.*
- **How It Works**:
  - Standard Google Analytics reports can take several hours to process incoming store data.
  - Enabling debug mode streams event data instantly into the **Google Analytics DebugView** tool.
  - This allows store administrators and vendors to verify that product views and test purchases are working correctly in real time.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/gc-4-debug.webp"><img src="./assets/gc-4-debug.webp" alt="GA-4 Debug Mode" /></a>

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/gc-4-debug-b.webp"><img src="./assets/gc-4-debug-b.webp" alt="Real-Time Purchase Data" /></a>

::: tip Recommended Practice
Keep Debug Mode enabled during store setup and initial testing. Once you verify that events appear properly in DebugView, you can leave it enabled or turn it off as preferred.
:::

---

## Vendor-Side Google Analytics Setup

When the administrator activates **Allow vendor to use Google Analytics**, sellers can connect their personal Google Analytics account directly from their dashboard:

1. The seller logs in and navigates to **Vendor Dashboard > My Profile**.
2. In the profile settings, the seller can configure:
   - **Google Analytics Account ID**: Enter their personal GA-4 Measurement ID (`G-XXXXXXXXXX`).
   - **Enable Tracking Events**:
     - Check **Enable view item event** to track visits to their products.
     - Check **Enable purchase event** to track completed sales and revenue for their products.
3. Click **Save Profile** to start tracking.

::: tip Multi-Vendor Order Attribution
If a customer places an order containing items from multiple vendors, the marketplace automatically attributes the relevant items and earnings to each vendor's individual analytics account.
:::

---

## Google Map API

- Admin can add the Google Map API key
- API key must be generated from the Google Cloud Console

- **Help Tip**: *Google Map API Key to be obtained form Google Account.*
- **Setup Guide**: <a href="https://webkul.com/blog/how-to-get-google-api-key/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Click here to know how to create one</a>.
- **Why It Is Used**:
  > *Although it is optional, but if filled top billing countries on vendor dashboard will be populated for all countries properly especially for US regions.*
- **Dashboard Benefits**:
  - Powers the interactive sales map displayed on the vendor dashboard.
  - Accurately plots customer billing countries and regional sales locations.
  - Ensures proper regional visualization for international orders and United States territories.

---

## Supported Analytics Data

The marketplace integration tracks comprehensive performance data to give you complete visibility over store activity:

### Product Performance

- Product revenue
- Unique purchases
- Quantity sold
- Average price
- Average quantity

### Sales Performance

- Transaction ID
- Revenue
- Tax
- Shipping cost

### Tracked E-Commerce Details

| Metric / Dimension | Tracked Event | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Product ID / SKU** | View Item, Purchase | Identifies the specific catalog product viewed or purchased. |
| **Product Name** | View Item, Purchase | The published title of the product. |
| **Price & Quantity** | View Item, Purchase | Product unit price and number of items purchased. |
| **Product Categories** | View Item, Purchase | Category hierarchy assigned to the product. |
| **Product Variations** | Purchase | Chosen variation attributes (e.g., Color, Size). |
| **Vendor / Brand** | Purchase | The seller shop or brand associated with the item. |
| **Order Number** | Purchase | Unique WooCommerce order confirmation ID. |
| **Total Revenue** | Purchase | Total monetary amount paid for the order. |
| **Tax & Shipping** | Purchase | Total tax and shipping costs associated with the order. |
| **Coupons** | Purchase | Any promotional discount codes used at checkout. |

---

## How to Verify Google Analytics on Your Store

To verify that your Google Analytics configuration is tracking accurately:

1. **Verify Live Events with DebugView**:
   - In your Google Analytics dashboard, navigate to **Admin > Data Display > DebugView**.
   - With **Enable debug mode** turned on in your marketplace settings, open a product page in a new browser tab.
   - Confirm that the `view_item` event appears in your DebugView timeline.
2. **Test Order Tracking**:
   - Place a test order on your marketplace.
   - When you reach the order confirmation page, verify that the `purchase` event is logged in DebugView along with the order value and purchased items.
3. **Use Google Tag Assistant**:
   - You can also use [Google Tag Assistant](https://tagassistant.google.com/) to confirm your Measurement ID is connected and actively sending hits.

---

# Configuration – Vendor Flags

The **Vendor Flags** feature allows customers to report vendors from their profile page.

The admin can manage this from:

**Marketplace > Settings > Vendor Flags**

**Direct Admin Navigation Paths**:
- **Settings Sub-tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_flags`
- **Reasons Sub-tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_flags#/reasons`

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-flags.webp"><img src="./assets/vendor-flags.webp" alt="Vendor Flags" /></a>

::: tip Profile Compatibility Note
Allow customers to report flags on the vendor profile. Please note that this feature is available on the legacy vendor profile layout.
:::

---

## Vendor Flags Overview

- Enables customers to report vendors for issues or concerns
- Helps maintain marketplace quality and trust
- Provides store administrators with early warnings about policy violations, inaccurate listings, or order fulfillment delays
- Promotes transparent and reliable seller operations across your marketplace

---

## Vendor Flags Settings Summary

The table below outlines the core configuration settings available on the Vendor Flags settings page:

| Setting Label | Input Type | Default Setting | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Enable** | Toggle Switch | Enabled | Turns the vendor flagging feature on or off across vendor profiles. |
| **Vendor Flag Text** | Text Field | `Report Vendor` | The label shown on the button or link that opens the reporting form. |
| **Guest Can Flag** | Toggle Switch | Enabled | Allows non-logged-in guest shoppers to submit vendor flag reports. |
| **Reason Required** | Toggle Switch | Enabled | Mandates that shoppers select or provide a reason before submitting a report. |
| **Accept Custom Reason** | Toggle Switch | Enabled | Permits shoppers to submit custom feedback beyond the predefined reasons list. |
| **Other Field's Placeholder** | Text Field | `Briefly describe the issue` | Guidance text displayed inside the custom reason input box. |

---

## Vendor Flags Settings

### Enable

- Toggle to enable or disable the vendor flag feature

- **How It Works**:
  - When enabled, a report button or link appears on public vendor store profiles.
  - When disabled, the reporting option is hidden completely from all vendor profiles, preventing new report submissions.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/marketplace-admin-setting-flag-setting.webp"><img src="./assets/marketplace-admin-setting-flag-setting.webp" alt="Marketplace Admin Setting Flag Setting" /></a>

---

### Vendor Flag Text

- Text displayed on the vendor profile for flagging
- Example: *Report this vendor*

- **Default Value**: `Report Vendor`
- **How It Works**:
  - Defines the clickable text or button label rendered on the vendor profile.
  - You can customize this label to fit your marketplace tone (such as *Report this vendor*, *Flag Seller*, or *Report an Issue*).

---

### Guest Can Flag

- Allows guest (non-logged-in) users to flag vendors

- **How It Works**:
  - **Enabled**: Unregistered visitors and guests can open the reporting modal and submit flags without signing in.
  - **Disabled**: Only logged-in customers can submit a flag report. Guests will be prompted to log in or register before submitting.

---

### Reason Required

- Forces customers to choose or specify a reason before submitting a flag

- **Default Value**: Enabled
- **How It Works**:
  - When active, the report form prevents submission until the customer selects a predefined flag reason or writes a custom explanation.
  - Helps prevent accidental submissions or empty complaints, ensuring every report contains meaningful feedback.

---

### Accept Other Reasons

- Enables customers to submit custom reasons
- Allows more detailed feedback beyond predefined options

- **Live Setting Label**: `Accept Custom Reason`
- **Default Value**: Enabled
- **How It Works**:
  - Adds an **Other** option to the flag reasons list.
  - When selected, a text input field opens where customers can describe specific issues that are not covered by predefined categories.

---

### Other Field Placeholder

- Text shown in the “Other Reason” input field
- Example: *Please specify your reason*

- **Live Setting Label**: `OTHER FIELD'S PLACEHOLDER`
- **Default Value**: `Briefly describe the issue`
- **How It Works**:
  - Sets the helpful placeholder text shown inside the custom text area to guide users on what information to provide.

---

## Vendor Flag Reasons

- Admin can manage predefined flag reasons
- Available actions:
  - Add new reasons
  - Edit existing reasons
  - Delete reasons

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-flags-reasons.webp"><img src="./assets/vendor-flags-reasons.webp" alt="Vendor Flag Reasons" /></a>

Marketplace administrators can access the reasons manager by clicking the **Reasons** sub-tab:

```text
Marketplace > Settings > Vendor Flags > Reasons
```

### Flag Reasons Table Reference

The Reasons management screen provides an interactive table listing all current flag categories:

| Column Header | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **ID** | Unique numerical identifier for the flag reason. |
| **Reason** | The text label presented to customers in the reporting form. |
| **Status** | A toggle switch allowing admins to quickly activate or deactivate individual reasons without deleting them. |
| **Created At** | Timestamp when the reason was created. |
| **Updated At** | Timestamp when the reason was last edited. |
| **Actions** | Dedicated buttons to **Edit** or **Delete** the reason. |

---

### Adding a New Flag Reason

To add a new predefined reporting reason:

1. Navigate to **Marketplace > Settings > Vendor Flags > Reasons**.
2. Click the **Add Reason** button in the top right corner.
3. In the **Add Reason** dialog:
   - **Reason**: Enter the descriptive reason text (e.g., *Unreasonable shipping delay*).
   - **Status**: Toggle the switch to make the reason active immediately.
4. Click **Submit** to save. The new reason will immediately become selectable on vendor profile report forms.

---

### Managing and Editing Reasons

- **Toggle Reason Status**: Use the toggle switch in the **Status** column to disable a reason temporarily without deleting historical reports.
- **Edit Reason**: Click the **Edit** button next to any reason to modify its wording or change its active status.
- **Delete Reason**: Click **Delete** to permanently remove a reason from the marketplace.

### Built-In Default Reasons

The marketplace includes several standard reasons ready for immediate use:

1. *Poor communication or unanswered messages*
2. *Repeated late dispatch*
3. *Item not as described*
4. *Unclear return or refund policy*
5. *Repeated order cancellations*
6. *Suspected counterfeit or resold goods*
7. *Misleading store or shipping information*
8. *Unresponsive to customer messages*
9. *Other*

---

## Admin Monitoring & Flag Count

Marketplace administrators can monitor vendor report volumes directly from the vendor directory:

1. In the WordPress admin menu, navigate to **Marketplace > Vendors**.
2. The vendors table includes a dedicated **Flag Count** column.
3. This column displays the total number of flags received by each vendor, helping admins quickly spot problematic sellers and conduct investigations.

---

## Customer-Side Reporting Workflow

When a shopper encounters an issue with a vendor:

1. The customer visits the seller's storefront profile.
2. Clicks the **Report Vendor** link or button.
3. A modal opens presenting the active predefined reasons.
4. The customer selects the matching reason (or chooses *Other* and types a custom explanation).
5. The customer clicks **Submit** to register the report with the marketplace administration.

# Configuration – Withdrawal

The **Withdrawal** feature allows vendors to withdraw their earnings using configured payment methods.

The admin can configure this from:

**Marketplace > Settings > Withdrawal**

**Direct Admin URL**:
```text
wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_withdrawal
```

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/withdrawal-settings.webp"><img src="./assets/withdrawal-settings.webp" alt="Admin Withdrawal Settings" /></a>

---

## Withdrawal Overview

- Enables vendors to withdraw their available balance
- Supports both manual and automatic withdrawal methods
- Admin can define limits, charges, and payment methods
- Helps maintain automated financial operations and transparent seller bookkeeping
- Automates fee deductions to offset payment processor transaction charges

---

## Withdrawal Settings Summary

The table below provides a quick reference for each setting on the Withdrawal configuration page:

| Setting Label | Input Type | Default Setting | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Enable Withdrawal** | Toggle Switch | Enabled | Turns the vendor withdrawal capability on or off across the marketplace. |
| **Withdrawal Limit (Minimum In $)** | Number Field | `50` | Minimum earnings balance required before a vendor can create a manual withdrawal request. |
| **Withdrawal Type** | Dropdown Selector | `Manual` | Sets whether payouts are initiated manually by vendors or processed automatically on schedule. |
| **Allow Request Payment From Order Listing** | Toggle Switch | Disabled | Adds a dedicated "Request Payment" button on completed orders in the vendor's order history. |
| **Withdrawal Methods** | Toggle Switches (Multiple) | Bank Transfer, PayPal, UPI Enabled | Controls which payout channels are available for vendors to receive their earnings. |
| **Withdrawal Charges** | Number Fields (Fixed + %) | Configured per Method | Sets flat and percentage fees deducted from payouts to cover transaction fees. |

---

## Withdrawal Settings

### Enable Withdrawal

- Toggle to enable or disable the withdrawal functionality for vendors

- **How It Works**:
  - When enabled, vendors gain access to the **Withdrawal** section in their vendor dashboard, allowing them to track withdrawable balances and submit payout requests.
  - When disabled, all withdrawal features are deactivated for vendors. Sellers cannot request payouts from the storefront, though existing transaction records remain intact in the admin ledger.

---

### Withdrawal Limit

- Minimum balance required to create a withdrawal request
- **Note:** This limit does not apply to automatic withdrawals

- **Default Value**: `50` (or equivalent in your active store currency)
- **How It Works**:
  - Vendors must accumulate earnings equal to or greater than this specified amount before they can submit a manual payout request.
  - Helps prevent high administrative overhead and excessive transaction fees caused by micro-withdrawals.

::: tip Automatic Payouts Exception
The minimum withdrawal limit applies **only** to manual withdrawal requests. When the marketplace runs automatic monthly payouts, all eligible settled balances are processed regardless of whether they meet this threshold.
:::

---

### Withdrawal Type

- Choose how withdrawals are processed:

#### Manual
- Vendors manually create withdrawal requests
- Vendors can:
  - Select eligible completed orders
  - Update withdrawal payment method
  - View applicable charges
  - See the final withdrawable amount before submitting

::: tip Vendor-Side Withdrawal
For step-by-step instructions on how sellers create and manage payout requests from their portal, see [Vendor Transaction Management](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-transaction-management.html).
:::

#### Allow Request Payment From Order Listing
- **Input Type**: Toggle Switch
- **Default Value**: Disabled
- **Live Help Text**: *Vendors get a Request Payment button on each completed order in their order list. Works with the Manual withdrawal type only.*
- **How It Works**:
  - When enabled alongside the **Manual** withdrawal type, a dedicated **Request Payment** action button appears directly next to completed orders in the vendor's **Orders History** (`vendor-orders`) list.
  - Sellers can quickly initiate payout requests for individual completed orders without manually navigating through the main withdrawal creation interface.

#### Automatic
- Withdrawal requests are auto-generated:
  - For all active vendors
  - On the last date of every month
- Vendors must select a default payment method
- Withdrawal charges (if any) are applied automatically

- **How It Works**:
  - The system automatically triggers a monthly batch payout calculation on the last calendar day of each month.
  - Payout requests are compiled for all active marketplace vendors who have accumulated withdrawable earnings and selected a default payment method.
  - Admin receives compiled payout lists ready for one-click bulk settlement via **Marketplace > Vendors Payout**.

---

### Withdrawal Method

- Enable or disable available withdrawal payment methods

The marketplace supports three primary payout channels that admins can enable or disable independently:

1. **Bank Transfer**
   - Enables direct bank wire transfers (ACH, NEFT, RTGS, SEPA, or BACS).
   - Vendors enter their Account Holder Name, Bank Name, Account Number, and Routing / IFSC / SWIFT Code in their profile.
2. **Paypal**
   - Enables electronic payouts directly to the vendor's registered PayPal account.
   - Vendors enter their PayPal email address in their profile.
3. **UPI**
   - Enables instant mobile payments through Unified Payments Interface.
   - Vendors provide their UPI Virtual Payment Address (VPA) / UPI ID (e.g., `vendor@bank`).

---

### Withdrawal Charges

- Define charges for each withdrawal method as required

To cover merchant processing fees or platform handling fees, the administrator can configure custom fee rules for each active payment method using a combined **Fixed ($) + Percentage (%)** model:

| Payment Method | Fixed Amount (`$`) | Percentage Amount (`%`) | Live Site Default Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bank Transfer** | Flat fee per request | Percentage of withdrawal amount | `$0` + `2%` |
| **Paypal** | Flat fee per request | Percentage of withdrawal amount | `$0.30` + `2.9%` |
| **UPI** | Flat fee per request | Percentage of withdrawal amount | `$0` + `1%` |

#### Calculation Example

If a vendor requests a **$200** payout via **PayPal** with configured charges of **$0.30 + 2.9%**:
- **Gross Request Amount**: $200.00
- **Percentage Charge (2.9%)**: $5.80
- **Fixed Charge**: $0.30
- **Total Deduction**: $6.10 ($0.30 + $5.80)
- **Net Amount Disbursed to Vendor**: **$193.90** ($200.00 - $6.10)

Vendors see a full transparent breakdown of applied charges before submitting their withdrawal request.

---

## Save Configuration

- Click **Save** to apply the withdrawal settings

1. Review your configured withdrawal limits, types, active methods, and charge structures.
2. Click the primary **Save** button at the bottom of the page.
3. A success confirmation confirms that the updated withdrawal policies are now live across your marketplace.

---

## Admin Payout Processing & Settlement

Once vendors submit withdrawal requests (or when automatic monthly requests generate), the marketplace administrator can review and settle payments from:

**Marketplace > Vendors Payout**

- **Centralized Dashboard**: Track total payable withdrawals, unpaid payout totals, and unpaid vendor counts.
- **Filter and Search**: Easily locate requests by vendor name, status (*Pending*, *Paid*), or unique Withdrawal ID.
- **Bulk Actions**: Select multiple pending requests and execute **Mark as Paid** or **Export CSV** for accounting records.
- **Individual Actions**: Click **Pay Now** to process and approve specific seller transactions immediately.

---

# Configuration – Vendor Invoice

The **Vendor Invoice** feature allows vendors to generate and share invoices for their orders, ensuring transparency between vendors, admin, and customers.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/admin-invoice.webp"><img src="./assets/admin-invoice.webp" alt="Vendor Invoice" /></a>

The admin can configure this section from:

**Marketplace > Settings > Vendor Invoice**

**Direct Admin URL**:
```text
wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=vendor_invoice
```

---

## Vendor Invoice Overview

- Allows vendors to generate invoices for their orders
- Helps maintain transparency in vendor earnings
- Invoices can be shared with customers as proof of purchase
- Both admin and vendors can send invoices to customers
- Provides verifiable accounting records for local tax, VAT, and business compliance
- Allows vendors to upload branded PDF or digital invoices directly from their dashboard
- Enables marketplace administrators to monitor, upload, download, and delete vendor invoices from the WordPress backend order editor

---

## Vendor Invoice Settings Summary

The table below provides a quick reference for each setting available on the Vendor Invoice configuration tab:

| Setting Label | Input Type | Default Setting | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Allow For Vendor** | Checkbox | Enabled (Checked) | Allows vendors to upload and manage custom invoices for their orders directly from the vendor dashboard. |
| **Attach in mail** | Checkbox | Enabled (Checked) | Automatically attaches uploaded vendor invoices to customer order notification emails. |
| **Allow File Types** | Multi-Select Dropdown | Blank (All supported types allowed) | Restricts uploaded invoice files to selected extensions (`jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `gif`, `pdf`, `doc`, `docx`, `ppt`, `pptx`). |
| **Allow File Size** | Number Field (KB) | `5000` KB (~5 MB) | Sets the maximum file size limit in kilobytes for invoice uploads (Minimum: `10` KB, Maximum: `20000` KB). |
| **Save Changes** | Primary Button | Click to Save | Stores and applies the updated configuration settings immediately across the marketplace. |

---

## Invoice Details Included

A vendor invoice contains the following information:

- Product price
- Vendor commission
- Shipping charges
- Applicable taxes
- Final vendor earnings
- Vendor shop name and seller contact details
- Customer billing and delivery addresses
- Order identification number and transaction date
- Itemized product quantities and subtotal amounts
- Payment gateway method and fulfillment status

---

## Vendor Invoice Settings

### Allow for the Vendor

- Enables vendors to generate and access invoices
- Invoices are available from the vendor dashboard

- **Control Type**: Checkbox (Toggle)
- **Default State**: Enabled (Checked)
- **Live Tooltip**: *"If checked then vendor can upload his invoice."*

#### How It Works:
- **When Enabled**: Vendors see a dedicated **Vendor Invoices** section on their order management page (`Order Details`). Sellers can name their invoice, choose a document from their local device, and save it.
- **When Disabled**: The invoice upload capability is hidden from the vendor dashboard. Vendors cannot attach custom invoices, but administrators can still manage invoices from the backend if necessary.

---

### Attach in the Mail

- Automatically attaches the invoice to order confirmation emails
- Ensures customers receive invoices without manual effort

- **Control Type**: Checkbox (Toggle)
- **Default State**: Enabled (Checked)
- **Live Tooltip**: *"If checked then uploaded invoices will be attach in customer order mail."*

#### How It Works:
- **Automated Delivery**: Once an invoice is uploaded by a vendor or administrator, the file is automatically attached to customer order transactional emails (such as order completed or order processing notifications).
- **Buyer Convenience**: Shoppers receive an official invoice document in their inbox immediately without having to contact customer support or log in to download it.
- **When Disabled**: Invoices are not sent as email attachments; buyers can still view and download them online by logging into their customer account.

---

### Allow File Types

- Defines the supported file formats for invoice uploads
- Common supported formats include:
  - PDF
  - JPG
  - webp

- **Control Type**: Multi-Select Dropdown with inline search (`Select File Types`)
- **Default State**: Blank (All supported formats accepted)
- **Live Tooltip**: *"Allow which file type user can attached invoice. If blank then user can upload any file type."*

#### Supported Format Options:
The dropdown selector includes the following file extensions:
- **Images**: `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `gif`
- **Documents**: `pdf`, `doc`, `docx`
- **Presentations**: `ppt`, `pptx`

::: tip Unrestricted Selection (Blank Field)
If the **Allow File Types** field is left blank with no specific formats selected, the marketplace automatically accepts any of the supported file formats listed above. To restrict uploads strictly to PDF documents, select only `pdf` from the dropdown.
:::

---

### Allow File Size

- Sets the maximum allowed file size for invoice attachments
- Helps manage storage and performance efficiently

- **Control Type**: Number Field (Input measured in Kilobytes - KB)
- **Default Value**: `5000` KB (~5 MB)
- **Allowed Range**: Minimum `10` KB to Maximum `20000` KB (~20 MB)
- **Live Tooltip**: *"Enter file size in KB. default is 5000 KB."*

#### Performance & Storage Protection:
- Prevents vendors from uploading excessively large files that consume server storage space.
- Ensures outgoing emails do not exceed standard mail server attachment size limits (which typically cap attachments between 10 MB and 25 MB).
- **Validation Check**: If an uploaded file exceeds the configured size limit, the system rejects the upload with an error prompt:
  ```text
  File size must not exceed {size} KB.
  ```

---

## Save Configuration

- After configuring the invoice settings, click **Save**
- Changes will apply immediately

- **Button**: Click **Save Changes** (`button button-primary`)
- The system updates the settings group (`wkmpsi-settings-group`) in the database, and the new rules apply instantly across the marketplace without requiring a server reboot or cache refresh.

---

## Vendor Invoice Management Workflow

### 1. Vendor Uploading an Invoice
1. The vendor logs in and navigates to **Vendor Dashboard > Orders**.
2. Opens an order in **View** mode.
3. Under the **Vendor Invoices** section:
   - Enters an **Invoice Name** (e.g., `Tax-Invoice-INV1024`).
   - Clicks **Choose File** and selects the invoice file from their computer.
   - Clicks **Save**.
4. The uploaded invoice appears in the order invoice table with:
   - **Invoice Name**
   - **Download Button** (downloads the file)
   - **View Button** (opens the file in a new browser tab)
   - **Delete Button** (removes the invoice if a correction is needed)

::: tip Vendor Invoice Upload Summary
- **Admin Configuration**: The marketplace admin must enable **Allow For Vendor** in the [Vendor Invoice Settings](#allow-for-the-vendor) for this upload section to appear on the seller dashboard.
- **Workflow Summary**:
  - **1. Access Order**: Navigate to **Vendor Dashboard > Orders** and click **View** on the specific order.
  - **2. Upload Document**: Enter a descriptive **Invoice Name**, select your file (such as a tax-compliant PDF or receipt), and click **Save**.
  - **3. Manage Files**: Use the **Download**, **View**, or **Delete** action buttons directly from the invoice list.
- **Storefront & Fulfillment**: For complete instructions on managing orders, tracking shipments, and handling customer fulfillment, refer to the [Vendor Order Management](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-order-management.html) guide.
:::

---

### 2. Admin Managing Invoices from WooCommerce Orders
Marketplace administrators can oversee and manage vendor invoices directly from the WordPress admin panel:

1. Navigate to **WooCommerce > Orders**.
2. Click on the target order to open the edit order screen.
3. In the **Vendor Invoices** meta box:
   - **Select Vendor**: Choose the specific vendor from the order.
   - **Invoice Name**: Enter a name for the document.
   - **Upload File**: Select and upload the file directly on behalf of the vendor.
   - **Actions Table**: View the **Shop Name**, **Invoice Name**, and action icons to **Download**, **View**, or **Delete** any attached invoice.

---

### 3. Customer Downloading Invoices
Customers can easily access their order invoices:

1. Customer logs in and goes to **My Account > Orders**.
2. Clicks **View** on the relevant order.
3. Above the order details table, the **Vendor Invoices** box displays all attached invoices:
   - Displays the **Shop Name** of the seller.
   - Displays the **Invoice Name**.
   - Provides **Download** and **View** buttons for instant access.

---

## Best Practices for Vendor Invoicing

::: tip Key Invoicing Recommendations
- **Enforce PDF Format as Primary**: While image formats (`jpg`, `png`) and office files (`docx`) are supported, configuring **PDF** as the main allowed format ensures invoices render consistently across all mobile and desktop devices and cannot be accidentally edited by buyers.
- **Maintain File Sizes Under 5000 KB**: Keeping the default `5000 KB` (5 MB) limit or setting it to `2000 KB` (2 MB) ensures rapid upload speeds for vendors, conserves server storage, and prevents email delivery failures caused by mail attachment limits.
- **Use Clear Invoice Naming**: Encourage vendors to use clear document titles (such as `INV-[OrderID]-[StoreName].pdf`) to make order records easy for customers and store accountants to identify.
- **Keep Mail Attachment Enabled**: Enabling **Attach in mail** delivers proof of purchase automatically to buyers upon order fulfillment, reducing customer support inquiries.
:::

- **[Vendor Invoice – Seller Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-invoice-view.html)**: Step-by-step user guide for vendors to view, generate, print, and download order invoices from the seller panel.
- **[Vendor Order Management](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-order-management.html)**: Guide on order tracking, order status updates, store pickup verification, and refund management.

# Configuration – Seller Central

The **Seller Central** settings allow the admin to configure and customize the **vendor onboarding page** for new sellers.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/sellercentral.webp"><img src="./assets/sellercentral.webp" alt="Seller Central" /></a>

The admin can access this section from:

**Marketplace > Settings > Seller Central**

**Direct Admin Navigation Paths**:
- **Banner Sub-tab (Default)**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_central` (or `#/`)
- **Features Sub-tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_central#/features`
- **Reviews Sub-tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_central#/reviews`
- **Workflow Sub-tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_central#/workflow`
- **Benefits Sub-tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_central#/benefits`
- **Registration Sub-tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_central#/registration`

**Live Storefront Endpoint**:
```text
https://your-domain.com/sellercentral/
```

::: tip Searchable Page Selectors & Slug Safety
The page selector for **Seller Central** is configured under **Marketplace > Settings > General**. Dropdowns for Vendor, Seller Central, and Terms & Conditions pages are searchable. To prevent routing conflicts, saving is blocked if two selectors point to the same page or if a selected slug conflicts with an existing marketplace endpoint.
:::

---

## Seller Central Overview

- Provides a dedicated onboarding page for new vendors
- Helps vendors understand marketplace features and benefits
- Improves vendor sign-up and conversion rate
- Fully customizable by the admin
- **Page Selectors**: Admins can easily select the Seller Central page. The selectors for Vendor, Seller Central, and Terms & Conditions pages are now **searchable**, making it easy to find the right page.
- **Collision Prevention**: To prevent issues, saving is automatically blocked if two selectors point to the same page, or if a selected page slug clashes with an existing marketplace endpoint.
- Serves as a high-converting recruitment portal to attract high-quality independent vendors to your marketplace.
- Centralizes content management for landing page copy, icons, testimonials, and registration labels without touching code or template files.
- Built on a reactive admin interface that updates settings in real time via the marketplace REST API (`/wp-json/wkmp_pro_api/v1/get_seller_central_settings`).
- Connects prospective sellers directly with the onboarding registration workflow, establishing merchant accounts in WooCommerce.

## Registration Section

- Allows the admin to configure vendor registration settings

### Registration Fields Configuration

The Registration sub-tab customizes the onboarding form rendered at the bottom of the Seller Central landing page. Admins can configure custom labels and placeholder text for each field:

1. **Registration Sub Title**: Enter instructional text or a welcome prompt displayed immediately above the registration input fields.
2. **Email ID**: Customize the label or placeholder for the vendor's primary login and notification email address.
3. **First Name**: Customize the placeholder text for the merchant representative's first name.
4. **Last Name**: Customize the placeholder text for the merchant representative's last name.
5. **Shop Name**: Customize the placeholder text for the public vendor storefront name.
6. **Shop URL**: Customize the placeholder text for the unique vendor shop slug (e.g., `https://your-domain.com/shop/vendor-slug`).
7. **Shop Phone**: Customize the placeholder text for the vendor's direct telephone contact number.
8. **Register Button Text**: Customize the call-to-action text displayed on the primary registration submission button.

### Registration Form Specifications Table

| Form Field | Input Type | Validation Rules | Profile Destination |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Email Address** | `email` | Required, Must be unique, Valid RFC format | WordPress User Account (`user_email`) |
| **First Name** | `text` | Required | WordPress User Meta (`first_name`) |
| **Last Name** | `text` | Required | WordPress User Meta (`last_name`) |
| **Shop Name** | `text` | Required, Unique marketplace storefront name | Vendor Shop Profile Meta (`shop_name`) |
| **Shop URL** | `text` | Required, Valid URL slug, Checked for slug collision | Public Vendor Store URL slug (`shop_url`) |
| **Phone Number** | `tel` | Optional / Recommended for business verification | Vendor Contact Information (`shop_phone`) |
| **Submit CTA** | `submit button` | Triggers client-side & server-side validation | Submits registration data for approval/activation |

::: tip Vendor Account Activation
Depending on the **Auto Approve Vendor** setting in **Marketplace > Settings > General**, new vendor submissions either gain immediate access to their vendor panel or enter a pending status awaiting administrator review under **Users > All Users** (filtered by the `Seller` role).
:::

## Connecting the Seller Central Page

To publish and display your customized Seller Central onboarding page on your storefront:

1. Navigate to **Pages > Add New** in WordPress.
2. Create a page with the title **Seller Central** (slug: `sellercentral` or `sell-with-us`).
3. Add the marketplace seller central block or shortcode, or set the page template as required by your theme.
4. Navigate to **Marketplace > Settings > General**.
5. Locate the **Seller Central** page selector dropdown.
6. Search and select your newly created **Seller Central** page.
7. Click **Save Changes** to bind the landing page endpoint.

::: tip Searchable Page Selectors
The dropdown selector is searchable. If your site has dozens of published pages, type the page title into the field to locate it instantly without scrolling through long option lists.
:::

## Best Practices for Seller Central & SEO

- **High-Impact Headline**: Craft a clear, benefit-oriented H1 banner heading that communicates the size and purchasing power of your customer base.
- **Optimized Visuals**: Use modern WebP or optimized PNG formats for all icons and banners. Keep icons uniform in size (e.g., 100x100 pixels) to avoid layout shifts.
- **Authentic Social Proof**: Include genuine testimonials with actual vendor names, store specialties, and professional headshots to build trust with new merchants.
- **Transparent Commission Messaging**: Explicitly highlight competitive commission rates in the Benefits section to overcome hesitation during sign-up.
- **Search Engine Optimization (SEO)**:
  - Add descriptive meta titles and meta descriptions using an SEO plugin (such as Yoast SEO or Rank Math) for the Seller Central landing page.
  - Target search terms like *"sell on [Your Marketplace Name]"*, *"become a marketplace vendor"*, and *"sell products online"*.
  - Keep the page slug clean and permanent (e.g., `/sellercentral/`).
- **Mobile Responsiveness**: Test your Seller Central page across mobile devices and tablets to verify that feature grids, testimonial sliders, and registration inputs render smoothly.

# Configuration – Vacation Settings

The **Vacation Settings** tab allows marketplace administrators to configure global vacation policies, customize closed-store button labels, control product visibility, and manage seller vacation schedules.

The marketplace admin can access and configure this section from:

**Marketplace > Settings > Vacation**

**Direct Admin Navigation URLs**:
- **Vacation Settings Tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=seller_vacation`
- **Vendors on Vacation Management**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-vacations`

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/admin-seller-vacation-settings.png"><img src="./assets/admin-seller-vacation-settings.png" alt="Admin Vacation Settings" /></a>

---

## Vacation Settings Overview

- Globally enable or disable the Vacation feature across the entire marketplace.
- Customize the Add to Cart button text displayed on single product detail pages when a store is closed.
- Customize the Add to Cart button label on category archives, shop loops, and catalog listing pages.
- Optionally hide products belonging to closed vendors from catalog listings, category archives, and search results.
- Automated daily scheduled task that automatically ends expired vacations and restores vendor stores.
- Centralized administrator control to monitor, enable, disable, edit, or delete any vendor's vacation schedule.

::: tip Vendor Guide Reference
To learn how vendors schedule and manage their holidays from the front-end seller dashboard, refer to the [Vacation Mode Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/vendor-vacation).
:::

---

## Admin Vacation Settings Summary

The table below provides a quick reference for each setting available on the **Vacation** configuration tab:

| Setting Label | Input Type | Default Setting | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Enable Vacation** | Checkbox | Enabled (Checked) | Allows vendors to use the Vacation feature. When disabled, the Vacation tab is hidden from vendor dashboards and no vacation restrictions are enforced on the storefront. |
| **Single Page 'Add to Cart' Button Label** | Text Field (Max 30 chars) | `Shop Closed` | Text displayed on the disabled Add to Cart button on the single product page when the vendor's shop is closed. |
| **Archive Page 'Add to Cart' Button Label** | Text Field (Max 60 chars) | `Currently Closed` | Text displayed on the Add to Cart button across shop, category archive, and catalog listing pages when the shop is closed. |
| **Hide Closed Products** | Checkbox | Disabled (Unchecked) | Hides closed-store products from shop, archive, and search results. Products remain visible on the vendor's profile page. Applies when a vendor blocks purchases during vacation. |
| **Automated Expiry Task** | Scheduled Task | Daily Automatic Execution | A built-in daily scheduled task that checks vacation end dates, ends expired vacations automatically, and reopens those vendor stores. |
| **Save Changes** | Primary Button | Click to Save | Immediately applies and stores the updated marketplace-wide vacation settings. |

---

## Admin Vacation Settings

### Enable Vacation

- **Setting Type**: Checkbox
- **Default State**: Enabled (Checked)
- **Live Description**: *"Allow vendors to use the Vacation feature. When disabled, the Vacation tab is hidden from vendors and no vacation rules are enforced on the storefront."*

#### How It Works:
- **When Enabled**: Vendors see the **Vacation** menu tab in their seller dashboard. Vendors can schedule vacations, configure custom notices, and manage store closure rules.
- **When Disabled**: The Vacation section is hidden from all vendor dashboards. Even if a vendor had previously saved a vacation period, no storefront restrictions (such as disabled Add to Cart buttons or product hiding) are enforced.

---

### Single Page 'Add to Cart' Button Label

- **Setting Type**: Text Field (Maximum 30 characters)
- **Default Value**: `Shop Closed`
- **Live Description**: *"Text on the disabled Add to Cart button on the single product page when the shop is closed. Maximum 30 characters."*

#### How It Works:
- When a vendor's vacation is active and configured to prevent sales, the standard **Add to Cart** button on the product details page (`PDP`) is disabled.
- The button text is replaced with this configured label (for example, *Shop Closed*, *On Vacation*, or *Temporarily Unavailable*).
- This clearly informs shoppers that the item cannot be purchased until the vendor returns.

---

### Archive Page 'Add to Cart' Button Label

- **Setting Type**: Text Field (Maximum 60 characters)
- **Default Value**: `Currently Closed`
- **Live Description**: *"Text on the Add to Cart button on shop / archive / listing pages when the shop is closed. Maximum 60 characters."*

#### How It Works:
- On catalog listing pages, category archives, tag results, and the main shop page (`PLP`), the Add to Cart button for products from closed vendors is updated to this custom label.
- This prevents customers from quick-adding products to their shopping cart from archive loops while a vendor is away.

---

### Hide Closed Products

- **Setting Type**: Checkbox
- **Default State**: Disabled (Unchecked)
- **Live Description**: *"Hide closed-store products from shop, archive and search results. Products stay visible on the vendor profile page. Applies only when a vendor blocks purchases during off hours."*

#### How It Works:
- **When Enabled**: Products belonging to vendors who are currently on vacation (with sales prevented) are filtered out from the main WooCommerce catalog, product category archives, and search results. Customers browsing the catalog only see purchasable items. Products remain visible when browsing the vendor's dedicated store profile page.
- **When Disabled**: Products from vacationing vendors remain visible in catalog and search results, but their Add to Cart button reflects the configured archive closed label and purchases are blocked.

::: tip Profile Visibility Note
Even when **Hide Closed Products** is enabled, products continue to display on the vendor's own store profile page (`/shop/vendor-name/`). This allows interested buyers to browse the seller's catalog and read the vacation return announcement.
:::

---

### Automated Vacation Expiry Task

- **Execution**: Daily Automatic Background Task
- **Live Note**: *"A daily scheduled task ends expired vacations automatically and reopens those shops."*

#### How It Works:
- The marketplace runs an automated daily scheduled task.
- It scans all active vacation records and checks whether the current date has passed the vendor's configured **To** date.
- When an expired vacation is detected, the system marks the vacation as **Expired**, removes all purchase blocks, and reopens the store automatically without requiring manual action by the vendor or administrator.

---

## Admin Controls for Vacation Mode

Admins have full control over the Vacation Mode feature:
- Enable or disable the vacation feature globally.
- Edit a specific vendor's vacation schedule and settings.
- Bulk enable, disable, or delete vacations from a sortable list in the admin panel.
- Customize the vendor dashboard URL endpoint for vacation.

### Managing Vendors on Vacation

Marketplace administrators can monitor all seller vacations from:

**Marketplace > Vacations**

**Direct Admin URL**:
```text
wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-vacations
```

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/admin-vacations-list.png"><img src="./assets/admin-vacations-list.png" alt="Admin Vendors on Vacation List" /></a>

#### List Features:
- **Status Filter Tabs**: Filter vacation records by **Active**, **Expired**, or **All**.
- **Information Columns**:
  - **Shop**: Name of the vendor's shop with quick action links (`Edit`).
  - **Vendor**: Display name and email address of the seller account.
  - **From**: Start date of the scheduled vacation.
  - **To**: Return date when the vacation concludes.
  - **Behavior**: Indicates whether the vendor chose to *Prevent sales* or *Keep shop open*.
  - **Status**: Current status of the vacation (*Active*, *Expired*, or *Disabled*).
- **Bulk Actions**: Select multiple vendors and apply **Enable**, **Disable**, or **Delete** with a single click.

---

### Editing a Vendor's Vacation from Admin

Administrators can directly inspect and modify any vendor's vacation schedule by navigating to:

**Marketplace > Vacations > Edit (Under Shop Name)**

**Direct Admin Edit URL**:
```text
wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-vacations&section=edit&vacation_id={ID}
```

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/admin-vacation-edit.png"><img src="./assets/admin-vacation-edit.png" alt="Admin Edit Vacation" /></a>

The Edit Vacation screen provides full administrative control over a seller's vacation dates, sales behavior, and customer-facing notice.

#### Edit Vacation Settings Summary

The table below outlines every parameter and input control available on the Edit Vacation screen:

| Setting Label | Input Type | Default / Values | Description & Operational Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Vendor** | Read-only Display | Shop Name & Email | Displays the seller shop name along with their account email address (e.g., `Lumen Beauty (hello@lumenbeauty.test)`). |
| **Enable vacation mode** | Checkbox | Checked / Unchecked | Admin override switch. Checking this immediately places the vendor into vacation mode across storefront pages. |
| **Schedule vacation mode** | Checkbox | Checked / Unchecked | When checked, displays calendar date pickers to constrain the vacation to a specific date range. |
| **Schedule: From** | Date Picker | Date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | Starting date when vacation mode begins taking effect. Required if schedule mode is active. |
| **Schedule: To** | Date Picker | Date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | Concluding date of the vacation. Must be identical to or later than the **From** date. |
| **During the vacation period** | Checkbox | Prevent sales (Default) | Controls purchasing behavior: Check to *"Prevent sales during vacation"* (blocks cart additions). Uncheck to keep the shop open for purchases while showing the message. |
| **Vacation message** | Rich Text Editor | Formatted Text / HTML | Custom announcement shown to customers on the vendor's profile banner and product pages while vacation mode is active. |
| **Update Vacation** | Primary Button | Click to Save | Applies the updated settings to the vendor's store immediately. |
| **Back to Vendors** | Button Link | Return to List | Cancels editing and returns the administrator to the main `Marketplace > Vacations` list. |

#### Detailed Edit Vacation Field Breakdown:

1. **Vendor Information**:
   - Identifies the specific vendor whose store is being managed. Displays both the public shop name and the registered user email address.

2. **Enable vacation mode**:
   - Allows administrators to instantly activate or deactivate vacation mode for this vendor, regardless of whether the vendor turned it on themselves.
   - When unchecked, the vendor's shop is immediately reopened and product purchase buttons return to normal.

3. **Schedule vacation mode (From & To Dates)**:
   - When checked, the schedule date inputs expand.
   - **Validation Rules**:
     - If scheduled mode is active, both **From** and **To** dates are required. If either date is missing, the system displays: *"Please provide both From and To dates for a scheduled vacation."*
     - The **To** date cannot be earlier than the **From** date. If an invalid date range is entered, the system prompts: *"The To date must be the same as or after the From date."*

4. **During the vacation period (Sales Behavior)**:
   - **Prevent Sales (Checked)**: Enforces purchasing blocks. On single product pages, the Add to Cart button is disabled with the configured closed label (e.g., `Shop Closed`). Archive pages reflect the closed state or hide the product based on marketplace settings.
   - **Keep Shop Open (Unchecked)**: The store continues taking customer orders. The custom vacation message still displays on the storefront, setting shopper expectations about fulfillment timelines while allowing ongoing revenue.

5. **Vacation message Editor**:
   - Uses the standard WordPress text editor with **Visual** and **Code** tabs.
   - Administrators can format text (bold, italic, bullet lists, blockquotes) and insert links.
   - This message renders prominently in the storefront vacation announcement banner on the vendor's profile page and individual product detail pages.

6. **Saving Changes**:
   - Clicking **Update Vacation** saves the modified vacation schedule and immediately applies the new rules across the marketplace storefront.
   - A success alert (*"1 vacation updated."*) confirms the update.

---

### Customizing the Vacation Endpoint URL

Store administrators can customize the vendor dashboard URL slug for the vacation section from:

**Marketplace > Settings > Endpoints**

- **Setting Name**: **Vacation**
- **Default URL Slug**: `vendor-vacation`
- **Vendor Dashboard Page**: `https://example.com/my-account/vendor-vacation/`

This allows administrators to tailor the dashboard URL structure to match their marketplace branding or multilingual setup without affecting vacation rules or seller data.

# Configuration – Staff Settings

The **Staff Settings** tab allows marketplace administrators to govern the sub-account (vendor staff) ecosystem. Admins can globally enable or disable the staff feature, set quotas on the maximum number of assistants each vendor may employ, define the global whitelist of delegatable capabilities across all marketplace modules (including Seller Dashboard, Products, Select And Sell, Bulk Upload, Orders, and more), and directly oversee, edit, or remove all vendor staff accounts across the marketplace.

The marketplace admin can access and configure this section from:

**Marketplace > Settings > Staffs**

**Direct Admin Navigation URLs**:
- **Staff Settings Tab**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-settings&tab=staff`
- **Vendor Staffs Management List**: `wp-admin/admin.php?page=wk-marketplace-vendor-staffs`

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/admin-staff-settings.png"><img src="./assets/admin-staff-settings.png" alt="Admin Staff Settings" /></a>

---

## Staff Settings Overview

- **Global Staff Control**: Enable or disable the vendor staff management feature across the entire marketplace.
- **Per-Vendor Staff Limits**: Configure maximum staff accounts allowed per vendor, or set to `0` for unlimited team members.
- **Granular Delegatable Permissions**: Control which permissions vendors are allowed to pass on to their staff across core modules and operational sections.
- **Consolidated Dashboard Permissions**: Manage access to the modern Seller Panel, store performance metrics, sales reports, customer lists, Magic AI tools, and storefront appearance from a unified Seller Dashboard card.
- **Select & Sell and Bulk Upload Controls**: Safely delegate existing catalog listing management and CSV batch processing to staff members.
- **Sensitive Permission Guardrails**: Critical capabilities (such as editing payment/payout information and managing KYC identity documents) are marked in red and left disabled by default for security.
- **Interactive Matrix Tools**: One-click **Select all** and **Deselect all** toggles on each capability card for rapid permission configuration.
- **Centralized Staff Registry**: Comprehensive admin list to review, search, sort, and bulk-delete vendor staff across all sellers.
- **Administrative Override & Editing**: Directly view and edit any staff member's profile details and fine-tune their individual permission set.
- **Per-Vendor Override**: Selectively enable or disable staff functionality for individual vendors through their seller profile, even when global staff access is disabled.
- **Customizable Dashboard Endpoint**: Tailor the front-end dashboard URL slug and menu title for the vendor staff section.

::: tip Vendor Guide Reference
To learn how vendors create staff accounts, assign roles, and delegate daily shop responsibilities from their seller dashboard, refer to the [Vendor Staff Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/vendor-staff).
:::

---

## Admin Staff Settings Summary

The table below provides a quick reference for each setting available on the **Staffs** configuration tab:

| Setting Label | Input Type | Default Setting | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Enable Vendor Staff** | Checkbox | Enabled (Checked) | Globally activates the vendor staff feature for all vendors. When disabled, only vendors individually enabled in their Miscellaneous/Seller settings can add staff. |
| **Max Staff Per Vendor** | Number Field | `0` (Unlimited) | Sets the maximum number of staff accounts an individual vendor can create. Set to `0` for unlimited staff members. |
| **Delegatable Permissions** | Interactive Card Grid | All Standard Checked (Sensitive Unchecked) | Defines the marketplace-wide pool of permissions vendors can delegate to staff. Vendors can only grant permissions enabled here. |
| **Save Changes** | Primary Button | Click to Save | Immediately applies and stores the updated global staff settings. |

---

## Admin Staff Settings

### Enable Vendor Staff

- **Setting Type**: Checkbox
- **Default State**: Enabled (Checked)
- **Live Description**: *"Allow vendors to add vendor staff staff. When off, only vendors individually enabled in their Miscellaneous settings can use it."*

#### How It Works:
- **When Enabled**: Every registered marketplace vendor gains access to the **Vendor Staff** menu in their front-end seller dashboard. Vendors can create sub-accounts, invite store assistants, and delegate daily operations.
- **When Disabled**: The **Vendor Staff** tab is hidden from seller dashboards across the marketplace. Existing staff members cannot log in to perform restricted seller actions.
- **Per-Vendor Exception Mode**: If the global setting is disabled, administrators can still selectively allow trusted or enterprise vendors to create staff accounts by enabling the permission within the vendor's individual **Seller Details** settings under **Marketplace > Sellers**.

---

### Max Staff Per Vendor

- **Setting Type**: Number Field
- **Default Value**: `0`
- **Live Description**: *"0 means unlimited."*

#### How It Works:
- **Unlimited Quota (`0`)**: Vendors can register as many staff members as their operations require without system restriction.
- **Numeric Limit (`1, 2, 5, etc.`)**: Caps the number of active staff accounts a vendor can maintain. 
- When a vendor reaches the configured limit, the seller dashboard disables the **Add Staff** action and notifies the vendor that their account allocation is exhausted.
- This setting is valuable for marketplace owners offering tiered membership plans (e.g., Free sellers receive 1 staff account, while Premium sellers enjoy expanded allocations).

---

### Delegatable Permissions Matrix

- **Setting Type**: Collapsible Capability Cards with Select/Deselect Controls
- **Live Description**: *"Permissions a vendor may delegate to staff. Vendors pick per staff from this set. Permissions shown in red are sensitive and are not granted by default."*

#### Operational Hierarchy:
The **Delegatable Permissions** setting acts as a master security boundary for the entire marketplace:
1. **Admin Master Whitelist**: Marketplace admins select the broad pool of capabilities that are safe for vendors to delegate.
2. **Vendor Sub-Assignment**: When vendors create or edit an assistant in their dashboard, they can *only* choose from the capabilities permitted by the admin here.
3. If an admin unchecks a permission here, it is automatically revoked from all vendor staff members, even if a vendor previously selected it.

#### Capability Modules & Permissions Breakdown:

The matrix is organized into clean functional cards matching the marketplace architecture:

| Functional Section | Capability Name | Sensitivity & Default Status | Operational Description |
