# Vacation Mode

The **Vacation Mode** allows vendors to temporarily close their store when they are unavailable. When enabled, the storefront displays a vacation notice with the vendor's custom message and blocks customer purchases.

::: tip Store Administration Note
If you are a marketplace administrator looking to configure global vacation policies, button labels, or backend overrides, please refer to the [Configuration – Vacation Settings](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/admin-vacation-setting) guide.
:::

---

## Accessing the Vacation Section

Vendors can manage their holiday schedules directly from the seller panel:

1. Log in to your **Vendor Account**.
2. From the seller dashboard sidebar navigation, click **Vacation**.
3. You will be directed to the **Vacation Overview** page (`/seller/vendor-vacation/`).

---

## Managing the Vacation List

The Vacation dashboard displays all scheduled, active, and past store breaks in an organized table.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vacation-list.png"><img src="./assets/vacation-list.png" alt="Vacation List" /></a>

### Status Filter Tabs

Above the vacation table, vendors can filter records using status tabs with dynamic counters:

- **All**: Displays all created vacation records, including active, inactive, and expired entries.
- **Active**: Filters only the vacations that are currently ongoing.
- **Expired**: Lists past vacations whose scheduled end dates have already passed.

::: tip Vacation Mode vs. Store Hours
At the top of the vacation table, you will see a helpful recommendation:  
*“Need to set daily opening & closing times instead? Manage them in Store Hours.”*

- **Vacation Mode**: Use this for temporary absences, holiday periods, or emergency closures (either on specific dates or indefinite manual breaks).
- **Store Hours**: Use this under your Vendor Profile to set regular daily opening and closing hours for recurring business schedules.
:::

### Vacation Table Columns

The table provides clear details for each vacation record:

| Column | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Checkbox** | Select one or more rows to perform bulk operations. |
| **Status** | Shows the current status badge: `Active` (green), `Inactive` (gray), or `Expired` (orange/red). |
| **Schedule** | Displays the vacation duration. If no end date was chosen, it shows `No end date (manual)`. If scheduled, it displays the date range (for example: `May 20, 2026 → June 2, 2026`). |
| **During vacation** | Indicates customer sales behavior: `Keep shop open` or `Prevent sales during vacation`. |
| **Last updated** | The exact date and timestamp when the vacation record was created or last updated. |
| **Actions** | Quick action controls including **Edit** and **Delete**. |

### Using Bulk Actions

Vendors can manage multiple vacation records at once using the bulk action bar:

1. Select the checkboxes next to the vacation records you want to update (or click the top header checkbox to select all).
2. Click the **Bulk actions** dropdown menu and choose one of the following:
   - **Enable**: Instantly turns on vacation mode for selected entries.
   - **Disable**: Deactivates vacation mode for selected entries.
   - **Delete**: Permanently removes selected vacation records.
3. Click the **Apply** button to confirm and execute the change.

---

## Adding a Vacation

To schedule a new break or close your store temporarily, click the **+ Add Vacation** button located at the top right of the vacation page.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/add-vacation.png"><img src="./assets/add-vacation.png" alt="Add Vacation" /></a>

The vacation settings form allows vendors to configure the following settings:

### 1. Enable Vacation Mode
- **Toggle Switch**: Turn this toggle ON to set your shop in vacation mode. Turn it OFF to keep your shop in normal operating mode.

### 2. Schedule Vacation Mode
- **Toggle Switch**: Enable this toggle if you want the vacation to run automatically for a specific date range.
- **Manual Mode (Toggle OFF)**: If left turned off, the vacation remains active continuously with no preset end date (`No end date (manual)`) until you manually return and turn it off.
- **Scheduled Mode (Toggle ON)**: When enabled, the date selection fields appear:
  - **From**: Choose the starting date of your vacation using the calendar picker.
  - **To**: Choose the ending date of your vacation. When this date passes, the store automatically reopens.

### 3. During Vacation Period (Sales Behavior)
Control how your storefront behaves during your absence:
- **Prevent sales during vacation (Toggle ON)**: Customers cannot purchase items from your store. Single product pages and catalog listings disable the Add to Cart button and show the marketplace closed label.
- **Keep shop open (Toggle OFF)**: Customers can continue placing orders normally. The custom vacation banner remains visible across your store to notify buyers of potential processing or shipping delays.

### 4. Vacation Message
- Enter a clear announcement text for your buyers in the rich-text editor.
- The editor supports both **Visual** and **Code** tabs, allowing you to format text with bold, italics, links, blockquotes, and lists.
- This message appears prominently on your vendor store profile banner and single product pages.

### Saving the Vacation
- Click **Save Vacation** to activate and save your new schedule.
- Click **Cancel** or the **Back** button at the top if you wish to return to the vacation list without saving.

---

## Editing a Vacation

Vendors can update an existing vacation schedule at any time:

1. From the Vacation list, find the vacation entry and click **Edit** under the **Actions** column.
2. The **Edit Vacation** page opens (`?section=settings&vacation_id=<id>`) with all previous details pre-filled.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/edit-vacation.png"><img src="./assets/edit-vacation.png" alt="Edit Vacation" /></a>

Vendors can modify existing schedules at any time:
- Adjust vacation start or return dates if plans change.
- Update the custom vacation announcement message.
- Toggle sales prevention on or off during an ongoing break.
- Disable vacation mode early to reopen the store before the scheduled end date.
- Click **Update Vacation** to apply the changes, or click **Cancel** to discard edits.

---

## Deleting a Vacation

Vendors can remove vacation records that are no longer needed:

- **Single Record Deletion**: In the Vacation table, click the **Delete** button under the **Actions** column for that row. A confirmation dialog will prompt: *"Delete this vacation?"*. Click **OK** to confirm removal.
- **Bulk Deletion**: Check the boxes next to the vacation records, select **Delete** from the **Bulk actions** dropdown, and click **Apply**.

---

## Storefront Behavior & Customer Experience

When a vendor initiates a vacation, the marketplace automatically reflects the seller's status across their store:

1. **Vendor Store Profile Banner**:
   - A dedicated notice banner appears at the top of the vendor's store page.
   - Displays the vendor's custom announcement (for example: *"We are away on holiday from Dec 20 to Jan 2. Orders placed now will be processed upon our return."*).

2. **Single Product Pages (`PDP`)**:
   - A vacation announcement alert appears on the product detail page.
   - If sales prevention is activated, the Add to Cart button is disabled and displays the marketplace closed label (such as `Shop Closed`).

3. **Product Catalog & Archive Pages (`PLP`)**:
   - Product cards display the archive closed label (such as `Currently Closed`).
   - If the marketplace administrator has enabled closed product hiding, products from closed vendors are filtered out from catalog listings and search results until the vacation concludes.

4. **Automated Store Reopening**:
   - Once the vacation end date passes, the marketplace's automated daily task restores the vendor's store to normal operating status and re-enables customer purchases.

---

## Best Practices for Vacation Mode

- **Schedule in Advance**: Plan vacations several days before departure to allow sufficient time to package and ship pending customer orders.
- **Provide Clear Dates**: Include expected return dates and order dispatch timelines in your custom vacation message to set realistic expectations for buyers.
- **Fulfill Existing Commitments**: Complete and mark open orders as dispatched before stepping away to keep fulfillment metrics and customer satisfaction ratings high.
- **Keep Shop Open for Pre-Orders**: If you manufacture products or accept advance backorders, consider leaving sales enabled with a clear notice explaining when shipping will resume.

---

<!-- source: https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-staff.html -->

# Vendor Staff

The **Vendor Staff** feature allows vendors to add sub-users (store managers and team assistants) who can log in and manage the store on their behalf. Vendors can grant per-task permissions for each section (view, add, edit, delete, and more) based on the capabilities allowed by the admin.

::: tip Store Administration Note
If you are a marketplace administrator looking to configure global staff settings, maximum staff limits per vendor, delegatable permissions, or manage all vendor staff members, please refer to the [Configuration – Staff Settings](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/admin-staff-setting) guide.
:::

---

## Why Use Vendor Staff?

Running a busy online store often requires teamwork. The Vendor Staff feature provides several practical advantages for sellers:

- **Secure Delegation Without Password Sharing**: Vendors do not need to share their master account password with assistants. Each staff member receives their own unique login.
- **Granular Permission Control**: Assign precise responsibilities to team members. For example, allow a shipping coordinator to view orders and print invoices without allowing them to delete products or issue refunds.
- **Role Specialization**: Create different sub-accounts for different team roles, such as product managers, customer support agents, order fulfillment staff, or designers.
- **Financial Privacy**: Staff members cannot view or modify the vendor's sensitive bank account details, payout settings, or withdrawal records.

---

## Managing Vendor Staff

Vendors can view a list of all their staff members from the Vendor Dashboard by navigating to **Vendor Staff** from the seller menu.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-staff-list.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-staff-list.png" alt="Vendor Staff List" /></a>

### Staff Directory Table

The main directory table displays the following columns for every registered assistant:

- **Name**: The full name of the staff member.
- **Email**: The staff member's registered email address used for signing into their account.
- **Access**: A comma-separated list of all marketplace sections and modules the staff member is permitted to access (such as *Seller Dashboard, Products, Orders, Transactions, Vacation, Shop Followers, Notifications, My Profile, Ask Admin, Shippings, Admin News*).
- **Actions**: Operational buttons available for each staff entry:
  - **Edit**: Opens the staff settings screen to change the staff member's name or adjust their permissions.
  - **Delete**: Permanently removes the staff member and revokes their store access.

---

### Adding a New Staff Member

To add a new staff member, click on the **+Add Vendor Staff** button located at the top right of the staff directory.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/add-vendor-staff.png"><img src="./assets/add-vendor-staff.png" alt="Add Vendor Staff" /></a>

On the **Add Vendor Staff** form, complete the required account details:

1. **Name**: Enter the staff member's full name (e.g., *Jane Doe*). This field is required.
2. **Email**: Enter their valid email address (e.g., *name@example.com*). This email is required and serves as their username for logging into the store.
3. **Choose Permissions**: Review the permission cards below the user details and select the specific tasks this staff member is allowed to perform.
4. **Save Account**: Click the **Add Vendor Staff** button at the bottom of the page to create the sub-account. To cancel without saving, click **Cancel**.

::: info Account Login Credentials
Vendors do not set a password manually when creating a staff account. An automatic email notification is sent to the staff member's email address with instructions to set up their password and log in.
:::

---

### Editing Staff Settings and Permissions

Vendors can edit existing staff settings and define precise permissions for what the staff member is allowed to do. To edit an assistant, click the **Edit** button next to their name in the staff directory table.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/edit-vedor-staff-setting.png"><img src="./assets/edit-vedor-staff-setting.png" alt="Edit Vendor Staff Setting" /></a>

When editing a staff member:

- **Name**: Can be updated at any time.
- **Email**: This field is locked (read-only) to protect user identity and maintain account security.
- **Permissions**: Check or uncheck capability checkboxes across the various permission cards to grant or revoke specific rights.
- **Update Changes**: Click the **Update Vendor Staff** button to apply the changes immediately.

---

### Removing a Staff Member

When a team member leaves or no longer requires access, vendors can delete their sub-account directly from the staff directory list:

1. Locate the staff member in the table and click the **Delete** button under **Actions**.
2. A confirmation modal titled **Remove vendor staff?** will appear.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-staff-delete-modal.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-staff-delete-modal.png" alt="Remove Vendor Staff Confirmation Modal" /></a>

3. Review the warning notice: *"This vendor staff will lose access to your store. This action cannot be undone."*
4. Click **Yes, remove** to confirm deletion, or click **Cancel** to keep the staff account.

---

## Granular Permissions Matrix

The permissions can be granularly controlled per section (e.g., Products, Orders, Profile) and per action (e.g., view, add, edit, delete). Each module is presented as a distinct card with an interactive **Select all** button on the header for quick configuration.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/allowed-staff-to-do.png"><img src="./assets/allowed-staff-to-do.png" alt="Allowed Staff Permissions" /></a>

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/allowed-staff-to-do-2.png"><img src="./assets/allowed-staff-to-do-2.png" alt="Allowed Staff Permissions Continued" /></a>

Here is the complete breakdown of all available permission cards and what each capability allows:

### 1. Seller Dashboard
- **Access New Seller Panel**: Allows logging in and navigating the modern seller dashboard interface.
- **Performance**: View store analytics, traffic metrics, and sales conversion figures.
- **Reporting**: Access comprehensive store reports and sales summaries.
- **Customers**: View customer listings and buyer information.
- **Magic AI**: Access built-in AI tools for product copy generation and content assistance.
- **General Setting**: Modify general shop configuration preferences.
- **Graph Setting**: Adjust dashboard graph display styles and color palettes.
- **Site Setting**: Customize storefront appearance preferences.

### 2. Products
- **View products**: Browse and view all products belonging to the vendor.
- **Add product**: Create new products in the vendor catalog.
- **Edit product**: Update existing product details, descriptions, prices, and inventory levels.
- **Delete product**: Remove products from the vendor's catalog.
- **Publish product**: Publish newly created or edited products live on the marketplace.
- **Generate barcodes**: Generate unique barcode labels for products.
- **Print barcodes**: Download and print generated product barcodes.

### 3. Select And Sell
- **View listing**: Browse existing catalog products available for selling.
- **Add product**: Join an existing product listing to offer the vendor's own price and stock.
- **Edit product**: Modify inventory, price, or product condition on assigned listings.
- **Delete product**: Remove the vendor's offer from an existing product listing.

### 4. Bulk Upload
- **Normal Products**: Batch upload standard catalog products using CSV data sheets.
- **Select And Sell**: Batch upload and map existing marketplace listings via CSV.

### 5. Orders
- **View orders**: View customer orders, ordered items, billing info, and shipping addresses.
- **Change order status**: Update order fulfillment statuses (e.g., Processing, Completed).
- **Refund order**: Process order refunds for the vendor's products.
- **Print invoice**: Generate and download printable customer invoices or packing slips.
- **Schedule pickups**: Book courier pickup appointments for store orders.

### 6. Transactions
- **View transaction list**: Review transaction history and balance ledger entries.
- **View transaction details**: Open individual transaction records to inspect itemized breakdowns.

### 7. Vacation
- **View vacations**: Check current, past, and upcoming store vacation schedules.
- **Add vacation**: Schedule a new store closure period with a custom storefront notice.
- **Edit vacation**: Modify dates or announcement text on existing vacation schedules.
- **Delete vacation**: Remove an existing vacation schedule to reopen the shop early.

### 8. Shop Followers
- **View followers**: See the list of registered customers who follow the vendor's shop.
- **Remove followers**: Remove specific customers from the followers list.
- **Send notification to followers**: Send email announcements or promotional updates to followers.

### 9. Notifications
- **View notifications**: Check real-time alerts for incoming orders, low stock, and system notices.

### 10. My Profile
- **View profile**: View public store profile details and settings.
- **Edit profile**: Update store biography, avatar, banner image, contact information, and social links.

### 11. Ask Admin
- **View query list**: Browse support inquiries sent to marketplace administrators.
- **View query thread**: Open an existing conversation thread to read admin replies.
- **Create new query**: Submit a new help ticket or question to the admin team.
- **Reply to query**: Post responses and follow-up questions in an ongoing support thread.

### 12. Shippings
- **View shipping**: View configured shipping methods and rates.
- **Manage shipping zones**: Create, edit, and configure custom vendor shipping zones and delivery rates.
- **Manage shipping classes**: Assign and organize product shipping classes.

### 13. Admin News
- **View news list**: Browse marketplace updates and announcements published by the admin.
- **View news details**: Read the full text of policy changes and marketplace news articles.

### 14. Storefront Design
- **View storefront layouts and variations**: Preview custom shop page designs and themes.
- **Customize and publish storefront designs**: Customize layout blocks, visual elements, and publish shop designs.

::: tip Fast Selection with "Select all"
Each capability card includes a **Select all** button in its header. Clicking this button instantly selects all permissions in that card. Clicking it again deselects all items, allowing vendors to quickly configure access.
:::

---

## Staff Member Dashboard Experience

Once a staff member logs into the marketplace using their credentials:

1. **Dynamic Navigation**: The seller dashboard menu automatically adjusts. The staff member only sees menu links for sections they are permitted to view.
2. **Action Restrictions**: If a staff member has permission to *View orders* but not *Refund order*, the refund action buttons remain hidden and inaccessible.
3. **Strict Account Isolation**: Staff members cannot access the primary vendor's bank account details, payout withdrawal forms, or administrative marketplace settings.
4. **Staff Management Restriction**: Staff members cannot create, edit, or delete other staff accounts. Only the primary vendor can manage sub-accounts.

---

## Staff Quotas and Admin Delegations

Please keep the following operational rules in mind:

- **Admin Delegatable Scope**: Vendors can only grant permissions that the marketplace administrator has enabled in the global delegatable capabilities list. If an admin turns off a specific capability globally, that permission is disabled for all staff.
- **Maximum Staff Limit**: The marketplace administrator may set a maximum number of staff accounts allowed per vendor (e.g., up to 5 assistants). If the limit is reached, the vendor must remove an existing assistant before adding a new one.

---

## Vendor Staff Quick Reference Summary

The following table provides a quick summary of the staff management workflow:

| Screen / Step | Action Button | Key Inputs | Outcome |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Staff List** (`/seller/vendor-staff/`) | **+Add Vendor Staff** | None | Opens the Add Vendor Staff form. |
| **Add Staff** (`?section=settings`) | **Add Vendor Staff** | Name, Email, Capability Checkboxes | Creates a new staff sub-account and sends login details to the assistant. |
| **Edit Staff** (`?section=settings&staff_id=XX`) | **Update Vendor Staff** | Name (editable), Email (read-only), Capability Checkboxes | Immediately updates the staff member's name and assigned permissions. |
| **Delete Staff** (Staff List Modal) | **Yes, remove** | Confirmation click | Permanently deletes the sub-account and revokes store access. |
| **Form Cancellation** | **Cancel** | None | Aborts current changes and returns to the staff directory list. |

---

## Vendor Staff Endpoint URL

Vendors access this management interface using the dedicated front-end endpoint:

```text
https://example.com/seller/vendor-staff/
```

*Note: Marketplace administrators can customize this endpoint slug and title under **Marketplace > Settings > Endpoints**. For more details, see [Endpoints Configuration](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/configuration-endpoints).*

# Product Management

Efficient catalog management is the foundation of any thriving multi-vendor marketplace. With WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace, vendors can easily add, organize, and monitor their products through an intuitive merchant interface, while marketplace administrators retain complete governance over publishing approvals, allowable product types, categories, and form presentations.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/product-management.webp"><img src="./assets/product-management.webp" alt="Product Management" /></a>

This guide covers the complete product management lifecycle: exploring the three product onboarding pathways, creating products using the guided 3-step wizard or the streamlined single-page form, utilizing the interactive **Listing Completeness** gauge, tailoring the form navigation layout in **Site Setting**, and navigating the product approval workflow.

---

## Accessing the Vendor Product List

Vendors access their central inventory by navigating to **Catalog > Products** in their merchant dashboard:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/product-list.webp"><img src="./assets/product-list.webp" alt="Vendor Product Catalog List" /></a>

### Catalog Table Data

The catalog table displays all products owned by or assigned to the vendor, along with vital operational details:

| Column | Information Displayed | Available Actions |
|---|---|---|
| **Image** | Product thumbnail image. | Visual identification of the catalog item. |
| **Product Name** | Product title and permalink. | Hovering displays quick action links: **Edit**, **View**, and **Duplicate**. |
| **SKU** | Stock Keeping Unit code. | Unique inventory reference. |
| **Stock** | Stock quantity and status badge (*In stock*, *Out of stock*, *On backorder*). | Real-time stock status check. |
| **Type** | WooCommerce product type badge (*Simple*, *Variable*, *Grouped*, *External*). | Identifies product architecture. |
| **Status** | Publication status badge (*Published*, *Draft*, *Waiting for Approval*, *Rejected*). | Displays live availability in the marketplace. |
| **Price** | Regular retail price and current active sale price. | Price validation and discount verification. |
| **Barcode** | Product barcode number and graphic representation. | Click **Download PNG** to save the vector barcode image. For variable products, click **Show variations** to view variation-specific barcodes. |

---

## Filtering the Catalog (12-Parameter Filter Drawer)

High-volume vendors managing extensive catalogs can locate specific inventory items instantly using the collapsible filter drawer.

Click the **Filter** button above the product table to open the slide-out drawer:

### Available Filter Criteria

The drawer provides 12 granular filter parameters to isolate products by title, SKU, pricing, taxonomies, approval stage, or barcode:

| Filter Parameter | Field Control | Available Values / Placeholder | Description & Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Name** | Text Input | `Name` | Partial or exact keyword match against the product title. |
| **SKU** | Text Input | `SKU` | Filters catalog items by parent product Stock Keeping Unit. |
| **Status** | Dropdown Select | *Draft*, *Waiting for Approval*, *Private*, *Published* | Filters listings by their publication status on the marketplace. |
| **Is Approved** | Dropdown Select | *Yes*, *No*, *Rejected* | Filters items based on administrator moderation review state. |
| **Draft Status** | Dropdown Select | *Yes*, *No* | Quickly isolates draft items from submitted listings. |
| **Type** | Dropdown Select | *Simple product*, *Grouped product*, *External/Affiliate product*, *Variable product* | Isolates catalog items by specific WooCommerce product architecture. |
| **Category** | Dropdown Select | Store categories (e.g., *Clothing*, *Decor*, *Music*) | Filters listings assigned to a specific catalog category. |
| **Price (Min / Max)** | Dual Numeric Inputs | `Min` and `Max` | Sets lower and upper price bounds ($) to locate items within a price bracket. |
| **Product Number** | Text Input | `Product or variation SKU` | Deep-searches across both parent products and individual variation SKUs. |
| **ID** | Numeric Input | `ID` | Locates an exact item by its unique WordPress database post ID. |
| **Barcode Value** | Text Input | `GTIN, UPC, EAN, or ISBN` | Searches inventory by global retail barcode or identification number. |

Click **Apply Filters** to update the catalog list. To reset the filter view, clear the drawer inputs and click **Apply Filters**.

---

## Bulk Catalog Actions

Vendors can perform batch operations on multiple products simultaneously to save administrative time:

1. Select individual products using the checkboxes in the first column, or check the header box to select all items on the page.
2. Select an operation from the **Bulk Actions** dropdown menu:
   - **Delete:** Moves selected products to the trash.
   - **Assign Categories:** Batch assigns chosen store categories across all selected items.
   - **Publish:** Submits selected draft items for immediate publication or administrative review.
   - **Generate Barcode:** Generates barcode graphics (*Code 128*, *EAN-13*, or *UPC-A*) for items with valid barcode numbers.
   - **Print Barcodes:** Compiles selected items into a formatted PDF label sheet ready for standard thermal label printers.
3. Click **Apply** to execute the bulk action.

---

        <div class="product-type-card__title">External / Affiliate</div>
        <span class="product-type-card__meta">Outbound Link</span>
      </div>
      <p class="product-type-card__desc">Listed here on the marketplace, but purchased and fulfilled on an external third-party website.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

3. Click **Next Step** (or scroll directly down if in single-page mode).

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/product-detail.webp"><img src="./assets/product-detail.webp" alt="Product Details" /></a>

The second stage captures product information, merchandising content, pricing, and logistics:

1. **Product Name & Magic AI Generation:**
   - **Product Name:** Enter a clear, keyword-rich title.
   - **Generate content (Magic AI):** Click the **Generate Content** button to open the Magic AI prompt dialog, allowing AI to draft compelling product titles, bullet points, and descriptions in seconds.
   - **Permalink Slug:** Vendors can review and customize the auto-generated URL slug.
2. **Descriptions:**
   - **Short Description:** Highlights displayed above the fold next to the primary image.
   - **Long Description:** Comprehensive specifications, materials, care guides, and warranty terms.
3. **Pricing:**
   - **Regular Price ($):** Standard retail price.
   - **Sale Price ($):** Optional promotional price with optional date schedule.
4. **Inventory & Identifiers:**
   - **SKU:** Unique merchant stock keeping unit.
   - **GTIN / UPC / EAN / ISBN:** Global barcode identifier. When populated, the system automatically renders the scannable vector barcode.
   - **Manage Stock:** Check to track numeric inventory counts.
   - **Stock Quantity:** Current on-hand quantity.
   - **Backorders:** Choose *Do not allow*, *Allow, but notify customer*, or *Allow*.
   - **Sold Individually:** Restricts customer purchases to 1 item per order.
   - **Maximum Purchasable Quantity:** Sets a quantity ceiling per customer cart.
5. **Media Uploads:**
   - **Featured Image:** Primary storefront image.
   - **Product Gallery:** Supplemental angles, packaging details, and lifestyle photography.
6. Click **Next Step**.

### 1. Product Stepper Toggle
- **Field Label:** `Product stepper`
- **Control:** Checkbox toggle (`wkmp_site_settings[show_stepper]`)
- **Description:** *"Show the Step 1–3 progress on the add and edit product screens."*
- **Usage:**
  - **Checked (Enabled):** Displays the guided Step 1, Step 2, and Step 3 progress bar on product creation and editing screens.
  - **Unchecked (Disabled):** Removes step banners and allows vendors to add products **in one go** on a unified page.

### 2. Listing Completeness Toggle
- **Field Label:** `Listing Completeness`
- **Control:** Checkbox toggle (`wkmp_site_settings[show_completeness]`)
- **Description:** *"Show the Listing Completeness score on the edit product screen."*
- **Usage:**
  - **Checked (Enabled):** Shows the real-time completeness percentage gauge and missing details checklist.
  - **Unchecked (Disabled):** Hides the gauge for power sellers who prefer a cleaner workspace.

### 3. Form Navigation Layouts
- **Field Label:** `Form navigation`
- **Control:** Dropdown selector (`wkmp_site_settings[layout]`)
- **Description:** *"Choose how the sections of the edit product form are laid out."*
- **Available Layouts:**

| Layout Option | Value | Visual Behavior & Ideal Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| **Horizontal Tabs** | `horizontal` | Sections (*Edit*, *Inventory*, *Shipping*, *Linked Products*, *Attributes*, *Tags & Brand*, *Status*) are rendered as clickable horizontal tabs across the top of the form. Best for standard screens and traditional tab navigation. |
| **Vertical Tabs** | `vertical` | Sections are aligned in a left-hand vertical menu column beside the active fields. Ideal for wide desktop monitors, providing quick one-click jumping between product components. |
| **Stacked Form** | `stack` | Sections are arranged continuously in stacked content cards on a single scrolling page. Ideal for laptop touchpads or rapid keyboard tabbing through every field without clicking tabs. |

Click **Save Changes** to apply preferences immediately across all product management screens.

---

## Managing Variable Products & Variations

When creating or editing a **Variable Product**, vendors can configure attribute matrices and manage individual variations:

1. In the **Attributes** tab, add attribute terms (e.g., *Color: Red, Blue, Green* or *Size: S, M, L, XL*). Check **Used for variations** and click **Save Attributes**.
2. In the **Variations** tab, click **Add Variation** or choose **Create variations from all attributes** to generate every possible combination automatically.
3. For each variation, customize:
   - Unique variation image
   - Variation SKU
   - Regular and sale pricing
   - Stock management and inventory count
   - Weight, dimensions, and shipping class
   - Unique GTIN / Barcode number *(See [Product Barcodes](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/product-barcode.html))*

---

## Product Approval & Rejection Workflow

When marketplace administrators require product review prior to publication, items follow a structured 4-stage review cycle:

1. **Submission:** When a vendor submits a product, its status is set to `Waiting for Approval` and it is hidden from storefront catalog listings.
2. **Administrative Review:** The administrator inspects the listing under **Marketplace > Product Approval**.
3. **Approval:** The administrator approves the product; its status switches to `Published` and it becomes visible on the storefront.
4. **Rejection with Reason:** If the listing violates guidelines or misses crucial details, the administrator clicks **Reject** and provides specific feedback in the rejection dialog. The vendor receives a notification detailing what must be corrected before resubmission.

---

## Admin Configuration: Product Rules & Governance

Marketplace administrators configure vendor catalog rules and form presentation from the WordPress administration panel:

Navigate to: **Marketplace > Settings > Product**

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/product-settings.webp"><img src="./assets/product-settings.webp" alt="Admin Marketplace Product Settings" /></a>

### Key Administrator Settings

| Setting Option | Description & Best Practice |
|---|---|
| **Allow Vendor to Publish** | When enabled, approved vendors can publish products directly without administrative review. Disable this if all items must be screened before going live. |
| **Allowed Product Types** | Select which WooCommerce product types (*Simple*, *Variable*, *Grouped*, *External*) vendors are permitted to create. |
| **Allowed Categories** | Restricts vendors to specific catalog categories, preventing miscategorization. |
| **Show Stepper** | Global default setting to show the Step 1–3 progress (Product Basics, Product Details, Complete Listing) on vendor add and edit product screens. |
| **Show Listing Completeness** | Global default setting to display the Listing Completeness score on the vendor's edit product screen. |
| **Form Navigation** | Sets the global default layout (*Horizontal Tabs*, *Vertical Tabs*, or *Stacked Form*) across all vendor accounts. |
| **Vendor Mode** | **Crucial Master Switch:** When checked, vendors see **Settings > Site Setting** in their panel, and their individual choice overrides the Product Form defaults for their own store. |
| **Allow Vendors to Bulk Upload** | Enables or disables CSV product import for vendor accounts. |
| **Maximum Rows per File** | Limits the maximum number of rows processed in a single CSV import (default: 500). |
| **Product Images (Bulk Upload)** | Determines image processing during bulk import (*Download image URLs*, *Vendor media library only*, or *No images*). |

# Manage Inventory

Accurate stock control is vital for every marketplace seller. Running out of stock leads to missed sales and dissatisfied buyers, while overstocking ties up valuable working capital. The **Manage Inventory** module in WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace gives sellers a centralized, high-speed workspace to update stock levels, edit SKUs and barcodes, track real-time sales metrics, and adjust quantities in bulk—all without opening the full product editor for every single item.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-inventory-dashboard.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-inventory-dashboard.png" alt="Vendor Manage Inventory Dashboard Overview" /></a>

This guide explains how to navigate the inventory dashboard, configure single-item stock rules inline, execute rapid bulk stock updates, utilize the 4-parameter filter drawer, and manage variation-level inventory for variable products.

---

## Accessing the Manage Inventory Screen

Vendors can reach the inventory management dashboard directly from their seller portal:

1. Log in to your merchant account.
2. In the left navigation menu, locate **Inventories**.
3. Click **Manage Inventory**.

The page resolves to the standard portal route:
```text
https://your-domain.com/seller/seller-manage-inventory/
```

> [!NOTE] Endpoint Customization
> Marketplace administrators can customize the frontend URL slug in **Marketplace > Settings > Endpoints**. By default, this screen uses the slug `seller-manage-inventory`.

---

## Inventory Dashboard & Product Overview

The Manage Inventory dashboard organizes catalog items into structured cards designed for fast scanning. Each card displays product details, operational order metrics, and current stock status at a glance.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-inventory-dashboard.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-inventory-dashboard.png" alt="Manage Inventory Dashboard Table and Metrics" /></a>

### Visible Data Fields & Quick Actions

| Data Field / Action | Displayed Information | Operational Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| **Product Image & Title** | Product thumbnail and catalog name. | Quick visual verification of the catalog item. |
| **SKU** | Stock Keeping Unit code (e.g., `XL-FAS-26`). | Unique identifier used for warehouse catalog tracking. |
| **Product Type** | Architecture badge (*Simple product*, *Variable product*, *Grouped product*, *External/Affiliate*). | Identifies whether the item has single or multiple inventory levels. |
| **Product ID** | System-assigned numeric ID prefixed with `#` (e.g., `#1021`, `#1174`). | Useful for customer support, queries, and quick system lookup. |
| **Current Price** | Active retail price or price range (e.g., `$34.00` or `$27.00 – $39.00`). | Immediate price reference without leaving the inventory view. |
| **Edit product** | Direct link to the complete product edit form. | Allows editing full descriptions, media galleries, categories, and attributes. |
| **Edit price** | Deep link to the Manage Pricing interface (`/seller/seller-manage-pricing/?wkmp_id=<id>`). | Opens targeted price and sale schedule controls for the item. |
| **Manage variations** | Available on variable products (e.g., *Manage 4 variations*). | Navigates to the variation inventory suite to manage stock per variation. |
| **Status Badge** | Publication badge (e.g., `Active`). | Confirms whether the product is currently visible on the live storefront. |
| **Date & Timestamp** | Creation or last modification timestamp. | Tracks catalog freshness and listing history. |
| **Sold** | Total units sold across fulfilled orders. | Tracks cumulative customer demand. |
| **Undelivered** | Units tied to active orders currently awaiting fulfillment or shipment. | Helps prevent overselling units that are already promised to buyers. |
| **Canceled** | Total units returned to available stock from canceled or refunded orders. | Assesses cancellation rates and return volume. |
| **Stock Badge** | Real-time stock status badge (*Stock: 22*, *Stock Not Managed*, or *Out of stock*). | Shows immediate operational inventory health. |
| **Manage inventory** | Primary toggle button. | Expands and collapses the inline inventory configuration panel. |

---

## Inline Inventory Configuration (Single Product)

Clicking **Manage inventory** on any product row expands a comprehensive configuration panel directly beneath the item without reloading the page.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-inventory-panel-expanded.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-inventory-panel-expanded.png" alt="Single Product Inline Inventory Configuration Panel" /></a>

### Configurable Inventory Settings

| Setting | Field Type | Placeholder / Defaults | Description & Best Practice |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SKU** | Text input | Enter unique SKU | Stock Keeping Unit code. Must be unique across your catalog to avoid synchronization issues. |
| **GTIN, UPC, EAN, or ISBN** | Text input | Barcode or unique ID | Global trade identifier barcode. Essential for multi-channel listings, Google Shopping feeds, and warehouse barcode scanning. |
| **Stock management** | Checkbox | `Track stock quantity for this product` | Enables automated WooCommerce inventory tracking. When unchecked, stock status is managed manually (*In stock* / *Out of stock*). |
| **Quantity** | Numeric input | Current quantity (e.g., `22`) | Available units on hand. For variable products, this acts as the fallback default for variations without manual stock rules. |
| **Allow backorders?** | Radio group | **Do not allow**<br>**Allow, but notify customer**<br>**Allow** | Governs checkout behavior when stock drops to zero or below:<br>• **Do not allow:** Blocks purchase when stock reaches 0.<br>• **Allow, but notify customer:** Allows order placement with a backorder notification on the cart/checkout.<br>• **Allow:** Silently accepts backorders as regular purchases. |
| **Low stock threshold** | Numeric input | `Store-wide threshold (2)` | Triggers an automated low-stock email alert when inventory falls to or below this number. Leave blank to adopt the marketplace store-wide default. |
| **Stock status** | Radio group | **In stock**<br>**Out of stock**<br>**On backorder** | Explicit manual stock indicator. Automatically switches if stock management is enabled. |
| **Sold individually** | Checkbox | `Limit purchases to 1 item per order` | Restricts buyers to purchasing only 1 unit per checkout order. Ideal for unique artwork, collectibles, or limited-run merchandise. |
| **Maximum Purchasable Quantity** | Numeric input | `Enter Maximum Purchasable Quantity` | Sets the maximum number of units a customer can place in their cart at one time. Protects inventory from rapid bulk buyouts. |

### How to Save Single-Product Changes

1. Click **Manage inventory** on the desired product row.
2. Update the stock quantity, SKU, barcode, or backorder settings as needed.
3. Click the **Save** button inside the panel.
4. The system validates and commits the updates immediately, updating the row's stock badge.

---

## Bulk Inventory Updates (Multi-Product Actions)

When updating stock for multiple catalog items at once—such as receiving a supplier shipment or marking seasonal items down—sellers can use the bulk action toolbar.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-inventory-bulk-actions.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-inventory-bulk-actions.png" alt="Bulk Inventory Updates Toolbar and Notifications" /></a>

### How to Perform a Bulk Stock Adjustment

1. **Select Products:** Check the checkbox next to each product you want to modify. To select all items on the current page, check the master checkbox in the header.
2. **Review the Selection Counter:** The toolbar displays the count of selected items (e.g., `Selected: 2`).
3. **Choose the Adjustment Action:** Select one of three calculation methods from the **Action** dropdown:
   - **Set to:** Replaces the current stock of all selected items with an absolute value (e.g., set all to `15`).
   - **Increase by:** Adds the specified quantity to the current stock level of each item (e.g., add `10` new units received from a shipment).
   - **Decrease by:** Subtracts the specified quantity from each item's current stock level (e.g., allocate `5` units to an offline sale).
4. **Enter the Value:** Type the numeric quantity in the **Value** input field.
5. **Click Apply:** The system calculates pending changes across selected rows and displays an informative banner:
   - **Products changed:** Number of products queued for update.
   - **Skipped notices:** If any selected product has stock management disabled, the system alerts you:
     > *Skipped X: stock is not tracked on those products (turn on stock management in their inventory settings, or change the parent product).*
6. **Save or Discard Changes:**
   - Click **Save Inventories** to commit all changes to the database permanently.
   - Click **Discard** if you want to cancel the pending changes and restore previous numbers.

> [!TIP] Restocking Shipments
> Always use **Increase by** when receiving stock replenishment shipments. This preserves existing unsold units and automatically adds incoming inventory without requiring manual math.

---

## Granular Search & 4-Parameter Filter Drawer

The Manage Inventory module includes instant search and a dedicated slide-out filter drawer to quickly isolate specific items within large product catalogs.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-inventory-filter-drawer.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-inventory-filter-drawer.png" alt="Slide-out Inventory Filter Drawer" /></a>

### Search and Display Controls

- **Live Keyword Search:** Type any keyword into the top **Search** box and press Enter to filter products by title or description.
- **Per Page Selector:** Choose how many items to display per page using the dropdown (`5`, `10`, `20`, `30`, `40`, or `50`).
- **Pagination Controls:** Navigate across large inventories using the bottom page pagination (`1`, `2`, `>`, `>|`).

### Filter Drawer Parameters

Click the **Filter** button in the upper toolbar to reveal the slide-out filter drawer:

| Filter Parameter | Control Type | Description & Usage |
|---|---|---|
| **SKU** | Text input | Filter products matching an exact or partial SKU code. |
| **Category** | Dropdown select | Select a catalog category (e.g., *Sports & Outdoors*, *Clothing*, *Accessories*, *Decor*) to view inventory for that department. |
| **Product Type** | Dropdown select | Filter by product structure: *Simple product*, *Grouped product*, *External/Affiliate product*, or *Variable product*. |
| **ID** | Numeric input | Filter directly by the unique numeric Product ID. |

After setting your criteria, click **Apply Filters** to refresh the list. To clear filters, remove the input values or close the drawer with the close icon (`✕`).

## Variable Products & Variation Inventory Management

Variable products contain multiple options (such as sizes, colors, or materials), each requiring distinct inventory tracking.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-inventory-variations-view.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-inventory-variations-view.png" alt="Variable Product Variation Inventory Management Suite" /></a>

### Parent Product vs. Variation Rules

On the main Manage Inventory list, variable products display a notification in their expanded configuration panel:

> *Settings below apply to all variations without manual stock management enabled.*

- **Parent-Level Stock:** If you track stock at the parent level, all variations share a single combined stock pool.
- **Variation-Level Stock:** If each color or size has separate warehouse stock, manage them individually through the variation suite.

### Opening Variation Inventory

1. On the main inventory list, find the variable product (e.g., *Cadence Water Bottle 750ml*).
2. Click the **Manage [X] variations** link (e.g., `Manage 4 variations`).
3. You are redirected to the dedicated variation inventory management screen:
   ```text
   /seller/seller-manage-inventory-variations/<product-id>/
   ```
4. Click **Back to Manage Inventory** in the breadcrumb trail whenever you need to return to the main catalog view.

### Variation Inventory Capabilities

The variation screen presents the parent product at the top, followed by each individual variation card (e.g., *Brushed Steel #77*, *Matte Black #78*, *Sand #79*, *Alpine Blue #80*):

- **Independent Variation SKUs:** Assign distinct barcode and SKU identifiers to every variation.
- **Variation Pricing Display:** View regular and active promotional sale prices for each specific option.
- **Specific Stock Quantities:** Manage exact stock counts for each size or color combination.
- **Variation Backorders & Low Stock Alerts:** Define separate backorder permissions and low stock alert thresholds for individual variations.

---

## Best Practices for Marketplace Sellers

- **Keep SKUs Unique and Systematic:** Use structured SKU conventions (e.g., `BRAND-CAT-ID-SIZE`) to prevent fulfillment errors and simplify inventory auditing.
- **Record Barcodes (GTIN/EAN):** Entering GTIN barcodes improves catalog searchability and ensures your items are ready for automated barcode scanner fulfillment.
- **Set Realistic Low Stock Thresholds:** Configure threshold amounts based on supplier restock lead times. If a product takes two weeks to restock, set the alert threshold to your average two-week sales volume.
- **Monitor the Undelivered Counter:** Always review the **Undelivered** column before making downward stock adjustments. Units marked as undelivered belong to pending orders and must not be sold again.
- **Use "Allow, but notify customer" for Fast-Moving Items:** If you have reliable suppliers, enabling backorders with customer notices maintains sales momentum during temporary out-of-stock periods without causing buyer confusion.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### Where do sellers find the Manage Inventory page?
In the seller dashboard, navigate to the left sidebar menu and click **Inventories > Manage Inventory** (URL route: `/seller/seller-manage-inventory/`).

### Can sellers update stock without opening the full product editor?
Yes. Click the **Manage inventory** button on any product row. An inline panel opens immediately, allowing you to update stock quantity, SKU, barcodes, backorders, and thresholds with a single click on **Save**.

### How does bulk stock adjustment work?
Check the boxes next to the items you want to update, choose **Set to**, **Increase by**, or **Decrease by** from the bulk toolbar, enter the numeric value, and click **Apply**. Verify the changes in the preview banner, then click **Save Inventories** to confirm.

### Why was a product skipped during bulk update?
A product is skipped if **Track stock quantity for this product** is turned off in its settings. To include it in bulk updates, expand the product's panel, enable stock management, and save.

### How do sellers manage stock for variable products like t-shirts with sizes?
Click the **Manage [X] variations** link on the variable product row. This opens the dedicated **Inventory Variations** page (`/seller/seller-manage-inventory-variations/<id>/`), where you can set individual stock counts, SKUs, and barcodes for each specific size and color.

### Can customers order more than the maximum purchasable quantity?
No. The **Maximum Purchasable Quantity** setting prevents any individual customer from adding more than the specified limit to their shopping cart in a single purchase.

# Selling Existing Products (Select & Sell)

In high-volume multi-vendor marketplaces, multiple merchants frequently offer identical brand-name goods, consumer electronics, books, or standard apparel. Creating separate product listings for every seller clutters the catalog, dilutes search engine ranking, and confuses shoppers with redundant duplicate pages.

**Selling Existing Products** (powered by **Select and Sell**) solves this by enabling multiple approved vendors to attach their own pricing, stock, and offer notes to a single master product in the marketplace catalog. Customers enjoy a clean storefront with side-by-side merchant comparisons, while vendors easily list catalog items without re-entering descriptions or uploading media.

---

## How It Works

<div class="creation-modes-banner" style="margin: 20px 0 24px 0;">
  <div class="creation-modes-banner__item">
    <h4><span>📦</span> Master Catalog Product</h4>
    <p>A single canonical catalog listing created by the marketplace administrator or an approved merchant, establishing master titles, product images, categories, and attributes.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="creation-modes-banner__item">
    <h4><span>🏷️</span> Multi-Seller Offer Layer</h4>
    <p>Multiple vendors attach competing offers to the same item—each specifying their own regular price, sale discount, stock count, and seller condition notes.</p>
  </div>
</div>

1. **Master Catalog Item:** A central product listing exists in the marketplace catalog with global images, categories, and descriptions.
2. **Vendor Offer Creation:** Approved vendors search the marketplace catalog, select the product, and define their own regular price, sale price, inventory quantity, condition description, and draft/publish status.
3. **Storefront Merchandising:** On the public product page, the marketplace displays the **lowest active price** by default, alongside the seller's custom note.
4. **Customer Comparison:** Shoppers can inspect all competing sellers via an inline comparison table or an interactive popup modal, choosing their preferred merchant based on price, shipping speed, or seller rating.
5. **Automatic Order Routing:** When an order is completed, revenue, tax, and commissions are automatically credited to the specific vendor whose offer was purchased.

---

## Listing an Existing Product (Select & Sell Flow)

Vendors attach offers to catalog items through a dedicated 2-step onboarding screen:

Navigate to: **Catalog > List Your Product** (`/seller/seller-list-product/`) &rarr; click **Search Products** (`/seller/seller-search-products/`).

Click the **Search Products** button to access the Select and Sell management console (`/seller/select-and-sell/`), then click **Add Product** (`/seller/add-selected-sell-product/`).

---

### Step 1: Select Category & Product Type

Select the taxonomy and architecture of the product you wish to sell:
- **Product categories:** Choose the category under which the target product is indexed (e.g., *Clothing*, *Accessories*, *Decor*, *Music*, *Sports & Outdoors*).
- **Product Type:** Choose between:
  - **Simple product:** Standard single physical or digital catalog item.
  - **Variable product:** Products with variations (e.g., sizes or colors).
- Click **Next Step** to proceed.

---

### Step 2: Select Product & Configure Offer Details

```
Catalog > Search Products > Add Product
[Select Product*] ──> Choose existing product from catalog
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Default Author Product Info                                 │
│ [Thumbnail] Product Price: $16.00  |  Stock Status: Instock │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Regular Price:   [ $14.50 ]
Sale Price:      [ $12.00 ]
Quantity:        [ 50     ]
Description:     [ Shown to customers below your price (0/300) ]
Status:          [ Draft / Publish ]
```

#### Field Specifications:

| Field Name | Type | Description & Merchant Usage |
|---|---|---|
| **Select Product\*** | Searchable Dropdown | Search and choose the specific marketplace product you want to sell (e.g., *Beanie with Logo*, *Long Sleeve Tee*, *Polo*). |
| **Default Author Product Info** | Preview Card | Displays the original author's baseline **Product Price** (e.g., `$16.00`) and real-time **Stock Status** (*Instock*). |
| **Regular Price** | Numeric ($) | Enter your custom retail selling price. Vendors can price competitively above or below the author's price. |
| **Sale Price** | Numeric ($) | Optional discounted promotional price. |
| **Quantity** | Integer | Enter the number of inventory units you currently hold in stock. |
| **Description** | Text Area (0/300) | Enter specific condition or offer details (*"Shown to customers below your price, for example the condition or what is included."*). Includes a live character counter. |
| **Status** | Selector | Choose **Draft** (saves privately in your vendor console to review later) or **Publish** (activates the offer immediately or submits it to the admin approval queue). |

Click **Save** to finalize your offer.

---

## Managing Your Offers (`/seller/select-and-sell/`)

Vendors manage all active offers under **Catalog > Search Products** (`/seller/select-and-sell/`):

- **Offer Data Table:**
  - **Image:** Master product thumbnail.
  - **Name:** Product title. Hovering reveals quick actions: **Edit**, **View** public product page, and **Delete**.
  - **Price:** Your active regular and sale price.
  - **Status:** Badge displaying *Publish*, *Draft*, or *Waiting for Approval*.
  - **Stock:** Current available units (e.g., *In stock (50)*).
- **Bulk Actions:** Select multiple offers using checkboxes and choose from the **Bulk Actions** menu:
  - **Delete:** Removes selected offers from the store.
  - **Set as publish:** Activates selected draft offers.
  - **Set as draft:** Temporarily hides selected offers from storefront customers.

---

## Storefront Presentation

On single product pages, customers can explore all participating merchants:

- **Primary Buy Box:** Displays the lowest price among all active sellers, along with that vendor's custom description note.
- **Other Sellers View:**
  - **Popup Modal Mode:** Clicking *"More Sellers"* opens an interactive modal window displaying merchant names, prices, feedback ratings, and individual **Add to Cart** buttons.
  - **List Table Mode:** An inline comparison table renders directly beneath the primary product details on the page.

---

## Admin Configuration & Governance

Marketplace administrators configure global Select & Sell settings, designate Global products, audit competing merchant offers, and moderate seller pricing from the WordPress dashboard:

Navigate to: **Marketplace > MP Select and Sell**

::: tip Complete Administrator Guide
For comprehensive instructions on managing Global vs Non-Global catalog items, search and filter controls, and administrative offer moderation, refer to the [Admin MP Select and Sell Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/admin-select-and-sell).
:::

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/product-settings.webp"><img src="./assets/product-settings.webp" alt="Select and Sell Admin Settings" /></a>

### Key Administrator Settings:

- **Enable MP Select and Sell:** Master toggle to activate multi-seller offer functionality across the platform.
- **Default Status As Global For All Products:** When enabled, all newly published products in the marketplace are automatically marked as Global, making them immediately available for other vendors to sell.
- **Seller Product Display Mode:** Choose between **Popup modal** or **List table** for customer comparison on single product pages.
- **Seller Email Notification:** Automatically sends an order confirmation email to the vendor whenever a customer purchases their specific offer.
- **Product Approval Queue:** When product moderation is active, newly submitted Select & Sell offers appear under **Marketplace > Product Approval**, where administrators can inspect offer details, approve, or reject with a formal reason.

# Bulk Upload (CSV Import & Export)

Manually entering products one by one can be time-consuming for brand distributors and high-volume merchants. WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace includes a high-performance **Bulk Upload** importer that enables vendors to create hundreds of new products or attach offers to existing catalog items in minutes using a single CSV spreadsheet.

This guide explains both bulk upload workflows, column mapping, file specifications, and catalog export for offline batch editing.

---

## Accessing the Bulk Upload Hub

Vendors access bulk management by opening:

**Catalog > Bulk Upload** (`/seller/seller-bulk-upload/`)

The console presents two specialized pathways:

```
Catalog > Bulk Upload
Choose how you want to add products in bulk.
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ List Your Own Products               │  │ Sell Catalog Products                │
│ Bulk create brand new products in    │  │ Add products already in the          │
│ your catalog from a spreadsheet.     │  │ marketplace catalog to your store,    │
│                                      │  │ at your own price and stock.         │
│ [ 4-Step Wizard: Upload/Map/Import ] │  │ [ 3-Step Wizard: Upload/Check/Done ] │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘  └──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

1. **List Your Own Products (`?import=products`):** Create brand-new products in your personal store catalog or update existing products using matching SKUs.
2. **Sell Catalog Products (`/seller/seller-bulk-sell-products/`):** Submit Select & Sell offers against existing marketplace products in bulk.

---

## Pathway A: List Your Own Products

Use this pathway to import completely new inventory or synchronize existing products in bulk via CSV.

Navigate to: **Catalog > Bulk Upload > List Your Own Products** (`/seller/seller-bulk-upload/?import=products`)

### Step 1: Upload a CSV file

- **Guidance:** *"Create new products, or update your existing ones, from a CSV file. Each row is checked against your store's rules, and you get a report for every row that could not be imported."*
- **Download CSV Template:** Click **Download CSV template** to obtain a ready-to-use CSV template containing all supported product fields:
  - `name`, `sku`, `type`, `regular_price`, `sale_price`, `manage_stock`, `stock_quantity`, `backorders`, `short_description`, `description`, `category_ids`, `tags`, `images`, `weight`, `length`, `width`, `height`.
- **File Dropzone:** Drag and drop your `.csv` spreadsheet (*"CSV only · up to 1 GB · at most 500 product rows"*).
- **Update existing products:** Check this box to update existing items whose SKU matches a row in the spreadsheet. When checked, you can choose whether non-matching rows create new products or are skipped.
- **Advanced Options:** Configure CSV field delimiter (comma `,`, semicolon `;`, or tab `\t`) and character encoding (`UTF-8`).
- **Continue:** Click **Continue** to proceed to Step 2 (**Map columns**).

---

### Export Your Products (Catalog Round-Tripping)

Directly beneath the upload dropzone, vendors can download their entire active catalog:

- **Guidance:** *"Download your products as a CSV in the same format. Edit prices, stock or details, then upload the file here with 'Update existing products' ticked. Products are matched by SKU, so a product without a SKU cannot be updated this way."*
- **Export Products Button:** Click **Export products** to instantly generate an offline CSV export of your active catalog. You can edit regular prices, sale prices, or stock counts in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets and re-upload the file with **Update existing products** ticked.

---

### Step 2: Intelligent Column Mapping

The importer reads your CSV header row and automatically pairs columns with WooCommerce product fields:

- **Automatic Pairing:** Recognizes standard headers such as *Product Name*, *SKU*, *Regular Price*, *Sale Price*, *Stock Quantity*, and *Categories*.
- **Manual Remapping:** For spreadsheets from external POS or ERP systems, use the dropdown menus to match spreadsheet columns to store attributes.
- **Ignore Column:** Set any irrelevant column to *Do not import* to omit it from processing.
- Click **Run the Importer** to proceed to Step 3.

---

### Step 3: Batch Import Processing

The import engine processes products in background batches:
- Live progress indicator tracks completion percentage.
- Validates categories against allowed marketplace taxonomies.
- Verifies product types against permitted seller permissions.

---

### Step 4: Import Results & Diagnostics

Upon completion, the system displays an import summary:
- **Imported:** Number of brand-new products added.
- **Updated:** Number of existing products synchronized.
- **Skipped / Failed:** Number of rows that encountered validation errors.
- **Download Error Report:** If any rows failed (e.g., duplicate SKU, missing title, or disallowed category), click to download a detailed CSV report specifying the row number and exact rejection reason.

---

## Pathway B: Sell Catalog Products (Bulk Select & Sell)

Use this pathway to attach Select & Sell offers to dozens or hundreds of admin-created products simultaneously.

You can check every row before anything is saved."*
- **Download CSV Template:** Click **Download CSV template** to receive a spreadsheet pre-populated with all master products currently eligible for Select & Sell in the marketplace. For variable products, the template includes one row per variation.

## Admin Configuration: Bulk Upload Settings

Marketplace administrators configure vendor bulk upload rules under:

**Marketplace > Settings > Product**

| Setting Option | Description & Best Practice |
|---|---|
| **Allow Vendors to Bulk Upload** | Master switch. When enabled, approved vendors see **Bulk Upload** in their panel. |
| **Maximum Rows per File** | Sets the maximum number of rows processed per CSV upload (default: `500`). Adjust based on server processing capacity. |
| **Product Images** | Controls image handling: **Download image URLs from the file** (downloads remote images to media library), **Only images already in vendor's media library**, or **No images** (added later manually). |

# Product Barcodes: Generation & Printing

In modern retail and warehouse fulfillment, physical barcodes are vital for fast inventory check-in, error-free order picking, and automated checkout scanning. WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace includes a built-in barcode engine that generates crisp vector barcodes for every product and variation, allowing vendors to print thermal label sheets directly from the seller panel.

This guide covers supported barcode formats, assigning barcodes to simple and variable products, batch PDF printing for thermal label printers, and staff permissions.

---

## Supported Barcode Formats

The marketplace engine supports three standard retail barcode symbologies:

| Format | Symbology Standard | Typical Use Case & Character Set |
|---|---|---|
| **Code 128** | High-density 1D barcode | Alphanumeric (letters, numbers, spaces, and punctuation). Standard for e-commerce packing slips, internal SKU tracking, and warehouse shelf bin locations. |
| **EAN-13** | International Article Number | 13-digit numeric standard used on retail consumer products worldwide outside North America. |
| **UPC-A** | Universal Product Code | 12-digit numeric standard used for retail point-of-sale in North America (USA and Canada). |

---

## Generating Barcodes on Products

Vendors can assign barcodes to individual products or generate them in bulk across the catalog.

### 1. Generating a Barcode on Single Products
1. Open any product for editing under **Catalog > Products** (`/seller/vendor-products/`).
2. Navigate to the **Inventory** tab (or **Edit** section depending on your form layout).
3. In the **GTIN, UPC, EAN, or ISBN** field, enter your numeric or alphanumeric identifier:
   - For retail items, enter the manufacturer-assigned GTIN, UPC-A, or EAN-13 number.
   - For custom or internal items, enter a custom unique SKU or code.
4. Click **Save Product** (or **Submit for Approval**).
5. The system automatically creates and renders the crisp vector barcode graphic below the field.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ GTIN, UPC, EAN, or ISBN: [ 8901234567890                  ] │
│                                                             │
│   || | |||| || ||||| ||| |||| | ||||| || ||| |||| ||        │
│                     8901234567890                           │
│   [ Download PNG ]                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

6. Click **Download PNG** to save the standalone high-resolution barcode image for product packaging, hangtags, or catalog design.

---

### 2. Barcodes for Variable Products
For products with multiple variations (e.g., sizes or colors):
- Open the **Variations** tab in the product editor.
- Each variation contains its own unique **GTIN / Barcode** input field.
- Vendors can assign distinct barcode numbers to each variation item (e.g., *Small/Red*, *Medium/Red*, *Large/Blue*).
- On the main **Products** list table, click **Show variations** in the Barcode column to view and download barcodes for every variation individually.

---

## Batch Barcode Generation & Printing

High-volume merchants can generate and print barcode labels for dozens of items simultaneously:

Navigate to: **Catalog > Products** (`/seller/vendor-products/`)

### 1. Bulk Barcode Generation
1. Select the products you want to generate barcodes for using the checkboxes in the first column.
2. Open the **Bulk Actions** menu and select **Generate Barcode**.
3. Choose the target symbology: **Code 128**, **EAN-13**, or **UPC-A**.
4. Click **Apply**. The engine generates and associates vector barcodes across all selected items.

---

### 2. Printing Barcode Label Sheets (PDF)
1. Select the checkboxes of the products or variations requiring physical labels.
2. In the **Bulk Actions** dropdown menu, select **Print Barcodes** and click **Apply**.
3. A formatted PDF document generates immediately in a new browser tab containing:
   - **Store Name:** Identifies the merchant / vendor.
   - **Product Title:** Complete item name and selected variation attributes (e.g., *German Premium Roast - 500g*).
   - **Retail Price:** Formatted price in the store currency.
   - **Vector Barcode Graphic:** High-contrast scannable lines rendered at 300 DPI.
   - **Alphanumeric Code:** Human-readable text beneath the bars.
4. Send the document directly to your thermal barcode printer (e.g., *Zebra*, *Rollo*, *DYMO*) or standard adhesive Avery label sheets.

---

## Filtering the Catalog by Barcode

Vendors can find specific products instantly using physical handheld barcode scanners:

1. On the **Products** catalog screen, click the **Filter** button to open the filter drawer.
2. Place the cursor in the **Barcode / GTIN** filter field.
3. Scan the physical product label using any USB or Bluetooth barcode scanner (or type the code).
4. Click **Apply Filters**. The catalog table updates immediately to display the exact matching item.

---

## Staff Permissions & Barcode Access Control

Store owners who employ team members can control who is authorized to view, generate, and print barcodes:

- Navigate to: **Vendor Staff > Permissions**
- Toggle the **Print Barcodes** permission:
  - **Enabled:** Staff members can generate barcode graphics and print label sheets during warehouse packing workflows.
  - **Disabled:** Hides barcode download and bulk printing tools from the staff member's interface.
