# Vendor Shipping Zone Management

In **WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace**, vendors have complete control over their shipping setup. Each vendor can create custom **Shipping Zones**, define targeted **Shipping Methods** (Flat Rate, Free Shipping, and Store Pickup), organize products with **Shipping Classes**, and configure **Local Pickup Locations** directly from their vendor panel.

::: warning Administrator Capability: Applicable Shipping Methods
For vendor shipping zones and rates to apply during customer checkout, the marketplace administrator must enable vendor shipping in the marketplace settings.

Under **Marketplace → Settings → General Settings → [Applicable Shipping Methods](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/configuration-general-settings#applicable-shipping-methods)**, the admin controls whether shipping is calculated globally or by individual sellers:
- **Vendor Shipping Method**: When enabled, the custom shipping zones, flat rates, free shipping rules, shipping classes, and local pickup locations configured on this page are active and apply to the vendor's products at checkout.
- **Admin Shipping Method**: When selected by the admin, global marketplace shipping rates apply to all products across the catalog, and individual vendor shipping rules are overridden.
- **Mixed Cart Calculation**: If a buyer orders items from both the admin and vendors, WooCommerce automatically combines the shipping rates at checkout.

For the marketplace administrator setup, please refer to the [General Settings – Applicable Shipping Methods](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/configuration-general-settings#applicable-shipping-methods) and [Shipping Settings Configuration](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/admin-configuration-shipping-settings) guides.
:::

---

## Accessing the Shippings Section

Vendors can manage their shipping operations from the seller dashboard:

1. Log in to your **Vendor Account**.
2. From the seller dashboard sidebar navigation, click **Shippings**.
3. You will arrive at the main **Shipping Overview** page (`/seller/vendor-shippings/`).

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-shippings-main.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-shippings-main.png" alt="Vendor Shipping Overview Table" /></a>

### Top Action Controls

At the top of the Shipping page, vendors have three quick action controls:

- **Add New Shipping Zone**: Opens the form to define a new geographic delivery zone.
- **Manage Shipping Classes**: Opens the table where vendors create class-based shipping groups (e.g., Heavy items, Fragile goods).
- **Manage Local Pickup**: Opens the local pickup configuration page and pickup location directory.

### Shipping Zones Table

The main table lists all delivery zones applicable to your store:

| Column | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Zone Name** | The recognizable title given to your shipping zone (e.g., *North America Zone*, *Domestic Delivery*). |
| **Region(s)** | The geographic areas covered by the zone, such as continents, countries, states, or specific ZIP codes. |
| **Shipping Method(s)** | The delivery methods currently active in this zone (e.g., *Flat rate*, *Free shipping*, *Store Pickup*). |
| **Actions** | Action icons to **Edit** (pencil icon) or **Delete** (trash icon) the zone. |

::: tip Rest of the World Zone
At the bottom of the table, you will see the default **Rest of the World** zone. This zone automatically applies to any customer whose address does not match any of your custom zones. Adding shipping methods to this zone is optional.
:::

---

## Adding a New Shipping Zone

To set up a new delivery region for your products:

1. On the **Shippings** page, click **Add New Shipping Zone**.
2. You will be redirected to the **Add Shipping Zone** page (`/seller/vendor-shippings/add/`).

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-add-shipping-zone.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-add-shipping-zone.png" alt="Add New Shipping Zone" /></a>

3. Configure the following zone details:
   - **Zone Name**: Enter a descriptive name for your shipping zone (e.g., *European Union*, *California Local*).
   - **Zone Region(s)**: Click the dropdown to search and select one or multiple regions (continents, countries, or individual states/provinces).
   - **Limit to specific ZIP/postcodes** (Optional): Click this link to open the postcode box if you want to narrow down the zone to specific postal codes.
     - Enter one postcode per line.
     - Wildcards (e.g., `CB23*`) and numeric ranges (e.g., `90210...99000`) are supported.
4. Click **Add shipping zone** to save your new zone.

::: note Adding Methods After Zone Creation
When creating a new zone, the shipping method section displays: *"You can add shipping method once you have create shipping zone."* Once the zone is saved, you can add and customize shipping methods from the zone edit page.
:::

---

## Editing a Shipping Zone & Adding Shipping Methods

After saving your shipping zone, you can manage the delivery methods offered within that region:

1. From the **Shippings** table, click the **Edit** (pencil) icon next to the zone you want to update.
2. The **Shipping Zone Edit** page opens (`/seller/vendor-shippings/{zone_id}/`).

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-edit-shipping-zone.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-edit-shipping-zone.png" alt="Edit Shipping Zone Page" /></a>

3. You can update the **Zone Name**, **Zone Regions**, or **ZIP/postcodes** at any time. Click **Update changes** to apply your updates.

---

## Adding a Shipping Method

To assign delivery methods to the selected zone:

1. Under the **Shipping Method** section of the edit page, click **Add shipping method**.
2. A popup window will appear asking you to choose a method.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-shipping-method-modal.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-shipping-method-modal.png" alt="Add Shipping Method Modal" /></a>

3. Select one of the available shipping methods from the dropdown list:
   - **Flat rate**: Charge a fixed fee per order or per item.
   - **Free shipping**: Offer zero-cost delivery based on coupons or minimum order amounts.
   - **Store Pickup**: Allow customers to collect their purchases from your store location.
4. Click **Add Shipping Method** to add it to the zone.

---

## Configuring Shipping Method Settings

Once a shipping method is added, click its name (e.g., **Flat rate**) to open its configuration settings.

### 1. Flat Rate Settings

The Flat Rate method lets you charge fixed or formula-based shipping fees:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-flat-rate-settings.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-flat-rate-settings.png" alt="Flat Rate Settings Modal" /></a>

- **Name**: The method title shown to customers at checkout (default: *Flat rate*).
- **Tax status**: Select whether this shipping fee is **Taxable** or has **None**.
- **Cost**: Enter the base shipping rate (excluding tax). You can enter a fixed number (e.g., `10.00`) or use advanced calculation syntax:
  - `[qty]`: Multiplies by the number of items (e.g., `10.00 * [qty]`).
  - `[cost]`: Total cost of items.
  - `[fee percent="10" min_fee="20"]`: Calculates a percentage-based fee with an optional minimum charge.
- **Shipping Class Costs**: If you have created shipping classes, individual cost fields appear for each class, along with the **Calculation type** (*Per class* or *Per order*).
- Click **Save Changes** to apply the configuration.

### 2. Free Shipping Settings

The Free Shipping method allows vendors to offer free delivery when specific requirements are met:

- **Name**: The label shown to buyers at checkout (default: *Free shipping*).
- **Free shipping requires**: Select the qualifying condition:
  - *No requirement*: Always free for this zone.
  - *A valid free shipping coupon*: Requires a promotional coupon.
  - *A minimum order amount*: Requires a minimum cart total.
  - *A minimum order amount OR coupon*: Either condition qualifies.
  - *A minimum order amount AND coupon*: Both conditions must be met.
- **Minimum order amount**: Enter the required minimum order value (e.g., `50`).
- **Coupons discounts**: Check **Apply minimum order rule before coupon discount** if the minimum amount should be evaluated before coupon deductions.
- Click **Save Changes**.

### 3. Store Pickup Settings

The Store Pickup method lets customers collect orders directly from your store:

- **Name**: The title displayed at checkout (default: *Store Pickup*).
- **Tax status**: Select **Taxable** or **None**.
- **Cost**: Optional collection fee (leave empty for free pickup).
- **Description**: Optional note displayed to customers with your store address (e.g., *"Please bring your order ID and photo ID for pickup"*).
- Click **Save Changes**.

### Deleting a Shipping Method

To remove a shipping method from a zone, hover over or click the small **Delete (×)** icon on the method badge, then confirm the removal.

---

## Managing Shipping Classes

Shipping classes help vendors group similar products and apply extra delivery charges (for example, heavier items or delicate products that need special packing).

To manage shipping classes:

1. Click **Manage Shipping Classes** from the main Shippings page, or navigate to `/seller/vendor-shippings/add-class/`.
2. The **Shipping Classes** management table will display.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-manage-shipping-classes.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-manage-shipping-classes.png" alt="Manage Shipping Classes Table" /></a>

### Adding a New Shipping Class

1. Click the **Add Row** button below the table. A new editable row will appear.
2. Fill in the following details:
   - **Shipping Class**: Enter a clear name (e.g., *Bulky & Heavy Items*, *Fragile Glassware*).
   - **Slug**: A unique URL-friendly slug (e.g., `bulky-heavy`). You may leave this blank to auto-generate from the name.
   - **Description**: An optional reference note explaining what products belong to this class.
3. The **Product Count** column will show how many products are currently linked to this class.
4. Click **Save Shipping Classes** to save your changes.

::: tip Linking Shipping Classes to Products
After saving a shipping class, edit any of your products under **Catalog → Products**. In the **Shipping** tab of the product editor, select your custom class from the **Shipping class** dropdown.
:::

---

## Managing Local Pickup & Pickup Locations

Vendors who operate physical retail stores, warehouses, or pickup counters can configure direct customer collection and manage multiple pickup points.

To access Local Pickup settings:

1. Click **Manage Local Pickup** from the main Shippings page, or navigate to `/seller/vendor-shippings/add-local/`.
2. The **Local Pickup** management page will open.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-manage-local-pickup.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-manage-local-pickup.png" alt="Manage Local Pickup Settings" /></a>

### 1. General Local Pickup Settings

At the top of the page, configure the general pickup preferences:

- **Enable local pickup**: Check this box to activate customer store pickup for your products.
- **Title**: The method title displayed during checkout (default: *Pickup*).
- **Cost**: Fixed fee for local pickup (leave blank for free customer pickup).
- **Taxes**: Choose whether pickup charges are **Taxable** or **None**.
- Click **Save Changes** to update these settings.

### 2. Adding a Pickup Location

Below the general settings, the **Pickup locations** table displays all active collection points.

1. Click the **Add pickup location** button.
2. The **Add pickup location** modal form will open:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-add-pickup-location-modal.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-add-pickup-location-modal.png" alt="Add Pickup Location Modal" /></a>

3. Enter the location information:
   - **Name**: The title of this location (e.g., *Downtown Retail Hub*, *Warehouse Store 2*).
   - **Address line 1 & 2**: Street address, building number, suite, or unit details.
   - **City, State, Postcode, Country**: Complete geographical details of the pickup counter.
   - **Pickup details**: Clear instructions for the customer (e.g., collection hours, parking directions, or required identification).
   - **Enabled**: Check this box to keep the pickup location active.
4. Click **Save Location** to save the pickup point.

The new location will appear in the **Pickup locations** table showing its Name, Address, Status (Enabled), and quick Actions to edit or remove it.

---

## Summary & Best Practices

| Feature | Where to Access | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shipping Zones** | `/seller/vendor-shippings/` | Group delivery regions (countries, states, postcodes) and assign shipping methods. |
| **Zone Methods** | Zone Edit Page (`.../vendor-shippings/{id}/`) | Set up Flat rate, Free shipping, and Store Pickup rates for each zone. |
| **Shipping Classes** | `/seller/vendor-shippings/add-class/` | Categorize items (e.g., heavy or fragile) and apply class-specific shipping costs. |
| **Local Pickup** | `/seller/vendor-shippings/add-local/` | Enable store pickup and list physical collection addresses for customers. |

- Always test your checkout flow after adding new zones to verify that the correct shipping rates and pickup options appear for customer addresses.
- Use postcodes with wildcards (e.g., `902*`) when offering localized flat rate or courier services within specific city districts.
- Ensure pickup instructions clearly state opening hours and documents required to provide a seamless collection experience for your buyers.

<!-- source: https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-order-management.html -->

# Vendor Order Management

In **WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace**, vendors have complete control over their incoming orders. Vendors can track new orders, filter them by fulfillment status, inspect line items and commission breakdowns, upload personalized tax invoices, update order statuses, verify store pickup security codes, and process refunds directly from their seller panel.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-orders-list-new.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-orders-list-new.png" alt="Vendor Order History List" /></a>

---

## Accessing Order History

Vendors can access their full order history from the dedicated seller panel:

1. Log in to your **Vendor Account**.
2. In the left navigation menu, navigate to **Sales > Order History**.
3. You will arrive at the main **Order History** page (`/seller/vendor-orders/`).

::: tip Admin Clause: Individual Vendor Settings & Order Approval
Marketplace administrators have the capability to manage individual rules and privileges for each seller under [Miscellaneous Settings (Vendor Level)](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-management-and-product-assignment.html#miscellaneous-settings-vendor-level).

If the administrator has activated the **Order Approval** clause for a specific vendor:
- Incoming customer orders will **only appear in the vendor's Order History after administrator review and approval**.
- Order notifications and buyer communication are released only after the admin approves the transaction.
- If a recently placed customer order is not yet visible in your **Order History**, it may be pending administrative approval as configured for your vendor profile.
:::

---

## Order Status Summary Cards & Quick Filters

At the top of the **Order History** page, vendors can see quick KPI summary cards showing real-time counts for every order status:

- **All Orders**: Total count of all orders containing your products (e.g., `25 All Orders`).
- **Processing**: Orders that are paid and awaiting shipment or fulfillment (e.g., `8 Processing`).
- **Completed**: Orders that have been delivered or fulfilled (e.g., `13 Completed`).
- **Pending payment**: Orders placed but waiting for customer payment confirmation (e.g., `0 Pending payment`).
- **Cancelled**: Orders cancelled by the customer or store admin (e.g., `2 Cancelled`).
- **Refunded**: Orders where funds have been returned to the customer (e.g., `0 Refunded`).

::: tip Instant One-Click Filtering
Click on any status card to filter the order table immediately. The active card is highlighted with a blue border, and the URL updates accordingly (for example, `/seller/vendor-orders/filter/processing/`). Click **All Orders** to return to the full list.
:::

---

## Search, Sort, and Advanced Filtering

Vendors can quickly find specific orders using search, sorting, and the slide-out filter drawer:

### Quick Search
- Enter an **Order ID** (e.g., `1171`) or **Product Name** in the **Search Orders/Products** input box.
- Press **Enter** or click the search icon to view matching results instantly.

### Sort By
Use the **Sort By** dropdown menu to reorder your order list:
- **Newest First**: Displays recently placed orders at the top (default).
- **Price - Low to high**: Sorts orders by gross amount in ascending order.
- **Price - High to low**: Sorts orders by gross amount in descending order.
- Click **Sort** to apply the selected order.

### Advanced Filter Drawer
Click the **Filter** button to open the slide-out filter drawer. This drawer allows vendors to combine multiple criteria:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-orders-filter-drawer.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-orders-filter-drawer.png" alt="Advanced Filter Drawer" /></a>

| Filter Field | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Order Id** | Search by exact order number (e.g., `1171`). |
| **Status** | Filter by order status (*All Orders*, *Processing*, *Completed*, *Pending payment*, *Cancelled*, *Refunded*). |
| **Date** | Quick presets: *Today*, *Yesterday*, *This Week*, *This Month*, *Last Month*, *Last 3 Months*, *Last 6 Months*, *This Year*. |
| **Custom Date Range** | Specify a custom range using **From date** and **To date** fields. |
| **Email** | Filter orders by the customer's billing email address. |
| **Customer** | Filter orders by customer's first or last name. |
| **Items** | Filter by item quantity range (**Minimum items** to **Maximum items**). |
| **Seller Earn** | Filter by vendor net earnings range (**Minimum seller earn** to **Maximum seller earn**). |
| **Payment** | Filter by payment gateway (*All payment methods*, *Cash on delivery*, *Check payments*, *Direct bank transfer*, *PayPal*). |
| **Shipment** | Filter by shipping method (*All shipping methods*, *Flat rate*, *Free shipping*, *Store Pickup*). |
| **Gross Amt.** | Filter by total order value (**Minimum gross amount** to **Maximum gross amount**). |
| **Discount** | Filter by coupon discount applied (**Minimum discount** to **Maximum discount**). |
| **Commission** | Filter by platform commission charged (**Minimum commission** to **Maximum commission**). |

Click **Apply Filters** at the bottom of the drawer to view filtered results.

---

## Order History Table Overview

The main table presents all relevant order details in an organized format:

| Column | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Order ID** | The unique order number (e.g., `#1171`). |
| **Order Date** | The date and exact time the order was placed by the customer. |
| **Order Status** | Current fulfillment state (e.g., `Processing`, `Completed`, `On hold`, `Cancelled`). |
| **Total Items** | Number of items purchased from the vendor's catalog in this order. |
| **Customer Name** | Full name of the customer. |
| **Withdraw Status** | Payout readiness of the funds for this order: <br>• **Available**: Funds can be withdrawn.<br>• **Requested**: Payout request submitted to admin.<br>• **Withdrawn**: Payout completed. |
| **Customer Address** | Full shipping or billing address of the customer. |
| **Total Amount** | The net amount credited to the vendor for this order after commission deductions. |
| **Action** | Action links: <br>• **View**: Opens full order details (`/seller/vendor-orders/{order_id}/`).<br>• **Store Pickup**: Quick access to pickup details for local collection orders. |

::: note Pagination
Vendors can navigate through multiple pages of orders using the page numbers (`1`, `2`) and arrow controls (`>`, `>|`) located below the table.
:::

---

## View Order Details

To inspect an order, click the **View** button in the **Action** column of any order row.

The single order view (`/seller/vendor-orders/{order_id}/`) provides comprehensive information and actions:

- **Back to orders**: Click this button at the top left to return to the **Order History** list.
- **Top Actions**: Action buttons located in the top-right corner:
  - **Refund**: Toggles the manual refund form for eligible items.
  - **Print Invoice**: Opens a print-friendly invoice in a new tab.
- **Order Notification Banner**: Highlights the order number, placement date, and current status (e.g., *Order #1171 was placed on October 21, 2026 and is currently Processing*).

### Order Items & Financial Breakdown

The items table displays each purchased item, associated SKU, quantity, and marketplace commission breakdown:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-order-items-summary.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-order-items-summary.png" alt="Order Items and Commission Summary" /></a>

- **Product & SKU**: Product title, variation, SKU, item quantity (`× 1`), and seller attribution.
- **Subtotal**: Product total before deductions.
- **Payment Method**: Gateway selected by the buyer (e.g., *Cash on delivery*, *PayPal*).
- **Admin Commission**: Marketplace fee deducted by the platform administrator.
- **Total**: Net earnings transferred to the vendor for this order.

### Customer Details

Displays essential contact and delivery details:
- **Email**: Customer's contact email.
- **Telephone**: Customer's phone number for delivery coordination.
- **Billing Address**: Registered billing address of the buyer.
- **Shipping Address**: Delivery destination for the items.

### Shipments (Courier Dispatch Tracking)

If items were dispatched through integrated courier fulfillment or manual carriers, the **Shipments** section displays:
- Shipment sequence and carrier method (e.g., *Shipment #1 — Fulfilment Carriers*).
- Dispatch timestamp.
- Dispatched product SKU and quantity.
- **Carrier Title** and **Tracking Number**.

---

## Upload Custom Invoice

Vendors can upload their personalized tax invoice file directly from the order details page if enabled by the platform administrator.

### Vendor Invoice Upload Steps

1. In the **Order Details** page, locate the **Vendor Invoices** section above the items table.
2. Enter a descriptive **Invoice Name** (e.g., `Tax-Invoice-INV1171`).
3. Click **Choose File** and select your invoice document (`PDF`, `JPG`, `PNG`, or `DOCX`) from your device.
4. Click **Save**.
5. Once saved, the invoice appears in the invoice table with:
   - **Invoice Name**
   - **Download Button**: Downloads the file to your computer.
   - **View Button**: Opens the file in a new browser tab.
   - **Delete Button**: Deletes the file if corrections are needed.

::: tip Vendor Invoice Upload Requirements
- **Admin Permission**: The marketplace admin must enable **Allow For Vendor** in [Configuration – Vendor Invoice](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/configuration-vendor-invoice.html).
- **Allowed Formats & Limits**: Invoices must match allowed file extensions and stay within the maximum file size limit (default: `5000 KB`).
- **Automatic Delivery**: If **Attach in mail** is enabled in marketplace settings, your uploaded invoice is automatically attached to order emails sent to the customer.
:::

---

## Update Order Status

Vendors can update the fulfillment status of their orders directly from the **Order Status** card:

1. Scroll to the **Order Status** section on the order details page.
2. Click the **Status** dropdown menu and select the new status:
   - **Pending payment**: Awaiting payment confirmation.
   - **Processing**: Payment received; order is ready for preparation and packing.
   - **On hold**: Order paused pending stock check or verification.
   - **Completed**: Order shipped, delivered, or picked up.
   - **Cancelled**: Order cancelled.
   - **Refunded**: Order refunded.
   - **Failed**: Payment failed.
   - **Draft**: Order draft state.
3. Click **Save** to commit the change.
4. The status update is automatically logged in the **Order Notes** section.

---

## Store Pickup OTP Verification

For orders placed with the **Store Pickup** shipping method, vendors verify customer collection directly from the order details page:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-order-pickup-verification.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-order-pickup-verification.png" alt="Store Pickup Verification Section" /></a>

1. Locate the **Pickup verification** section on the order page.
2. Review the store location address (e.g., *Aurora Athletics · 1420 SE Water Avenue, Suite 3, Portland, OR*).
3. Click **Send code**. The system generates a secure one-time verification PIN (OTP) and sends it directly to the customer's registered email address.
4. When the customer arrives at the store counter:
   - Ask the customer for the verification code received on their phone or email.
   - Enter the code into the verification input field and click **Verify code**.
5. Once verified, the order can safely be marked as **Completed**.

::: tip Security Advantage & Dedicated Guide
Store pickup OTP verification protects vendors against unauthorized collections and guarantees that only the verified buyer collects the merchandise.

For comprehensive instructions on managing local pickup orders, utilizing the search and filter drawer on `/seller/store-pickup/`, and delegating permissions to counter cashiers, refer to the [Vendor Store Pickup Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-store-pickup.html).
:::

---

## Generate Refund (Vendor End)

Vendors can generate refund requests for eligible orders directly from the order page:

### Steps to Generate a Refund

1. Open the order in **View** mode (`/seller/vendor-orders/{order_id}/`).
2. Click the **Refund** button in the top action bar. The button toggles to **Cancel**, and refund input columns appear in the items table.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-order-refund-interface.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-order-refund-interface.png" alt="Vendor Order Refund Interface" /></a>

3. Configure the refund details:
   - **Refund Quantity**: Enter the number of units to refund for each product line. The refund amount updates automatically.
   - **Refund Reason (Optional)**: Enter an explanation for the refund (e.g., *Customer requested cancellation*, *Item defective*).
   - **Restock refunded items**: Check this box if you want the refunded units added back into your available product stock.
   - **Refund Amount**: Review the calculated total refund amount.
4. Click **Refund Manually** to finalize the refund.

### Refund Confirmation
- Upon submission, a confirmation message **“Refunded successfully”** is displayed.
- The refunded line items and amounts are updated under the **Order Total** section.
- A permanent log entry is added to the **Order Notes**.

---

## Print Invoice

Vendors can generate a clean, printable customer invoice at any time:

1. Click the **Print Invoice** button in the top-right corner of the order details page.
2. The print invoice view opens in a new browser window (`/vendor/invoice/{encoded_order_id}`).
3. Vendors can preview the invoice, save it as a PDF, or send it directly to their printer.

For a comprehensive guide covering the full invoice layout, itemized commission calculations, print/PDF export, and custom tax invoice uploads, see the dedicated [Vendor Invoice User Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-invoice-view.html).

---

## Order Notes Timeline

The **Order Notes** card records a complete, chronological audit trail of all actions related to the order:

- **Customer Notification Logs**: Records transactional emails dispatched to the buyer.
- **Courier & Pickup Tracking**: Displays scheduled carrier collections, tracking numbers, and dispatch timestamps.
- **Stock Movements**: Records automated stock deductions and reservation holds (e.g., *Stock levels reduced: Aurora Training Tee (23→22)*).
- **Status History**: Logs every status change made by the vendor or system administrators.

---

## Schedule Pickup & Courier Fulfilment

For orders shipped with non-integrated shipping methods—such as **Free Shipping** or **Flat Rate**—vendors can record courier dispatch details and provide tracking numbers to customers directly from the order list:

- Eligible orders display a **Schedule Pickup** action link in the order history.
- Vendors review remaining quantities to ship, choose from administrator-approved couriers (e.g., DHL Express, FedEx Ground) or the manual **Self Ship** fallback, enter the parcel **Tracking ID**, and schedule the collection.
- Upon submission, an automated **Customer Note** is added to the order, triggering an email notification to the buyer containing the courier name and tracking code.

For complete administrative setup, carrier options, and staff capabilities, refer to the [Fulfilment Carriers Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/fulfilment-carriers).

## Summary

In WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace, the vendor order management workflow enables sellers to:

- Access and review all store orders under **Sales > Order History**.
- Understand administrative clauses such as **Order Approval** configured individually under [Miscellaneous Settings (Vendor Level)](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-management-and-product-assignment.html#miscellaneous-settings-vendor-level).
- Track order volumes instantly through **Order Status KPI Cards** (All Orders, Processing, Completed, Pending payment, Cancelled, Refunded).
- Filter orders with the **Search bar**, **Sort By dropdown**, and the **12-parameter Advanced Filter Drawer**.
- Inspect complete financial summaries showing **Subtotal**, **Payment Gateway**, **Admin Commission**, and **Net Seller Earnings**.
- Upload custom store invoices and print official marketplace order receipts.
- Update fulfillment statuses and securely verify local collections with **Store Pickup OTP Verification**.
- Process manual refunds with optional automated inventory restocking.
- Review transparent operational logs in the chronological **Order Notes** timeline.

# Vendor Store Pickup Management

In **WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace**, vendors can offer local in-store pickup to customers who prefer collecting their purchases directly from the vendor's physical store or warehouse. Store pickup eliminates shipping fees for buyers, provides faster access to goods, and drives direct foot traffic into the vendor's retail location.

To make local fulfillment smooth and secure, the seller portal includes a dedicated **Store Pickup Orders** management section. From here, vendors and their authorized store staff can track pickup queues in real time, filter incoming collections, send secure one-time verification codes (OTP) to buyers, verify customer identity at the counter, and safely finalize order handovers.

Vendors can access their store pickup dashboard directly from the seller portal menu:

**Store Pickup > Store Pickup Orders**

**Direct Seller Navigation URL**: `/seller/store-pickup/`

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-store-pickup-orders-list.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-store-pickup-orders-list.png" alt="Vendor Store Pickup Orders Management Dashboard" /></a>

---

## Store Pickup Dashboard Overview

The **Store Pickup Orders** workspace is designed specifically for front-desk cashiers, warehouse staff, and store owners managing customer collections. It separates local pickup fulfillment from traditional courier-shipped orders, giving vendors full clarity over ready-to-collect packages.

Key highlights of the vendor store pickup interface:

- **Dedicated Pickup Queue**: Displays only orders that were purchased using the **Store Pickup** delivery method.
- **Real-Time Collection Statuses**: Quickly distinguish between orders currently **Awaiting pickup** versus orders that have already been **Picked up**.
- **Customer Contact Visibility**: Displays the customer's full name and billing email address directly in each order row for instant customer verification.
- **Flexible Search & Filtering**: Locate any pickup order within seconds using the keyword search bar or the dedicated filter drawer with date range, order status, and pickup status options.
- **Configurable Table View**: Switch between `10`, `20`, or `50` order rows per page according to your daily collection volume.
- **Single-Click Order Drilldown**: Click **View** or the hyperlinked **Order ID** to access full order details, line items, customer addresses, and the OTP verification panel.
- **Mandatory OTP Handover Security**: Built-in fraud protection prevents orders from being marked as Completed until the customer's 6-digit verification code is confirmed at the counter.

::: tip Related Documentation
- **Order Management**: Learn how to manage general orders and invoices in the [Vendor Order Management Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-order-management.html).
- **Staff Delegation**: Learn how to assign pickup permissions to counter cashiers in the [Vendor Staff Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-staff.html).
- **Marketplace Settings**: Review platform-wide store pickup configurations in the [Admin Store Pickup Settings Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/store-pickup-settings.html).
:::

---

## Store Pickup Orders Table Breakdown

The main table on `/seller/store-pickup/` provides key operational information for every local collection:

| Column Header | What It Shows | Operational Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Order** | Displays the order number with a leading hash (e.g., `#1171`). | Clickable link that opens the detailed vendor order page (`/seller/vendor-orders/{order_id}/`). |
| **Date** | Displays the date and exact timestamp when the customer completed checkout (e.g., `October 21, 2026 11:45 am`). | Helps staff determine how long an order has been waiting for collection. |
| **Customer** | Shows the customer's full name on the top line and their billing email address underneath. | Used by counter staff to look up arriving customers and confirm contact details. |
| **Pickup store** | Displays the registered store name or retail branch where items must be collected (e.g., `Aurora Athletics`). | Ensures customers are collecting from the correct physical store location. |
| **Items** | Shows the total number of physical product units in the pickup order (e.g., `1`). | Helps warehouse and store staff quickly confirm package contents. |
| **Total** | Displays the total monetary amount of the order, formatted in your store currency (e.g., `$34.00`). | Confirms order total and payment status before releasing items. |
| **Order status** | The standard WooCommerce lifecycle status badge (*Processing*, *Completed*, *On hold*, *Cancelled*, etc.). | Indicates whether the order is paid and ready for handover. |
| **Pickup status** | The specific collection status badge: <br>• **Awaiting pickup**: Items are prepared, waiting for customer arrival.<br>• **Picked up**: Customer OTP was verified and goods were collected. | Clear visual cue showing whether physical handover has taken place. |
| **Actions** | Displays the **View** button. | Opens full order details to initiate the OTP code verification process. |

## Searching and Filtering Pickup Orders

During busy trading hours, front-counter staff need to locate arriving customers quickly. The store pickup interface provides both quick search and an advanced slide-out filter drawer.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-store-pickup-filter-drawer.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-store-pickup-filter-drawer.png" alt="Vendor Store Pickup Filter Drawer" /></a>

### 1. Quick Keyword Search
Located immediately above the table, the **Search** input allows instant lookups:
- Type an **Order ID** (e.g., `1171`).
- Type a **Customer Name** (e.g., `Demo Customer`).
- Type a **Customer Email** (e.g., `demo_customer@nexora.test`).
- Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to filter the table instantly to matching orders.

### 2. Slide-Out Filter Drawer
Click the **Filter** button (`wkmp-v2-filter-btn`) above the table to open the **Apply Filters** drawer. The drawer offers 4 specific criteria:

1. **Order status**:
   Filter orders according to their overall order state:
   - *Select* (All statuses)
   - *Pending payment*
   - *Processing* (standard state for paid orders awaiting customer pickup)
   - *On hold*
   - *Completed*
   - *Cancelled*
   - *Refunded*
   - *Failed*
   - *Draft*

2. **Pickup status**:
   Filter orders by collection progress:
   - *Select* (All pickup states)
   - *Awaiting pickup*: Shows only orders currently waiting for the customer to arrive at the store.
   - *Picked up*: Shows completed collections where OTP verification has already occurred.

3. **From Date**:
   Select the start date to view orders placed on or after this specific calendar day.

4. **To Date**:
   Select the end date to view orders placed on or before this specific calendar day.

Click **Apply Filters** at the bottom of the drawer to display the filtered results. To reset your view, open the drawer, clear the fields, and click **Apply Filters** again.

## In-Store Counter Handover & OTP Verification

To protect both the seller and the customer against lost packages or disputed collections, WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace incorporates a secure **One-Time Password (OTP)** verification system.

When a customer comes to collect their package, follow these step-by-step instructions on the order details page (`/seller/vendor-orders/{order_id}/`).

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-store-pickup-verification-box.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-store-pickup-verification-box.png" alt="Vendor Store Pickup Verification Card" /></a>

### The 5-Step Counter Handover Workflow

| Step Number | Stage Name | Who Does It | Action Description |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **01** | **Customer Arrival** | Customer & Staff | Customer arrives at the counter and provides their order number (`#1171`) or name. |
| **02** | **Send Verification Code** | Store Staff | Staff opens the order and clicks **Send code** to dispatch a secure 6-digit PIN to the buyer's email. |
| **03** | **Check Customer Email** | Customer | Customer opens their inbox on mobile and reads out or shows the 6-digit PIN. |
| **04** | **Verify Code at Counter** | Store Staff | Staff enters the code into the verification input and clicks **Verify**. |
| **05** | **Hand Over Goods & Complete** | Store Staff | Staff hands over items and updates order status to **Completed**. |

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-order-1171-pickup-detail.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-order-1171-pickup-detail.png" alt="Vendor Order Details with Store Pickup Verification" /></a>

### Detailed Handover Procedure:

#### 1. Locate the Order
Open **Store Pickup > Store Pickup Orders** and click **View** next to the customer's order. You can also open the order from **Sales > Order History** (`/seller/vendor-orders/`).

#### 2. Review Pickup Information
Scroll to the **Order Status** card on the right side of the screen. Underneath the status dropdown, locate the **Pickup verification** section:
- Verify the listed store location (e.g., *Aurora Athletics · 1420 SE Water Avenue, Suite 3, Portland, OR 97214*).
- Check that the order is currently in **Processing** status and paid.

#### 3. Click "Send code"
Click the **Send code** button (`wkmp-v2-btn js-wkmp-store-pickup-send`):
- The platform automatically generates a unique 6-digit one-time verification code.
- An email is instantly dispatched to the customer's registered billing email address containing the collection PIN and store details.
- A countdown timer appears indicating how long the code remains valid (configured by the administrator, such as 15 or 30 minutes).

#### 4. Enter and Validate Customer PIN
When the customer receives the email:
- Ask them to provide the 6-digit verification code shown on their device.
- Enter the code into the verification input field.
- Click **Verify code**.
- The system checks the code. Once authenticated, the pickup status changes to **Picked up**, and a success confirmation message appears.

#### 5. Save Order as Completed
With the customer verified and goods handed over:
- Change the **Status** dropdown from *Processing* to **Completed**.
- Click **Save**.
- The order is officially completed, and the transaction details are recorded in your store earnings and order audit notes.

---

## Mandatory Completion Guardrail

The marketplace provides an automated security safeguard to protect vendors from fulfilling orders prematurely:

::: warning Verification Required Before Completion
If a vendor or staff member attempts to change an unverified store pickup order to **Completed** and clicks **Save**, the system blocks the update and displays a reminder:

> *"The order must be verified before it can be completed. Send the customer a one-time code by email and ask for it at the store."*
:::

This guardrail guarantees that:
- Goods are never marked as collected before the customer actually visits the store.
- Counter staff remember to verify customer identity.
- Dispute risks and chargebacks are minimized because every collection has a verified audit trail.

---

## Delegating Store Pickup to Vendor Staff

If you employ store managers, warehouse workers, or counter cashiers, you do not need to share your main seller account login. You can create dedicated staff accounts with specific store pickup permissions.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-store-pickup-orders-list.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-store-pickup-orders-list.png" alt="Vendor Staff Pickup Access" /></a>

### Store Pickup Staff Capabilities

When setting up staff members under **Vendor Staff** (`/seller/vendor-staff/`), assign the following capabilities:

| Capability Name | What the Staff Member Can Do |
| :--- | :--- |
| **View store pickup orders** | Allows staff to log in, view the **Store Pickup Orders** menu, search for customers, and open pickup order details. |
| **Send and verify pickup codes** | Authorizes counter staff to click **Send code**, view the verification box, enter customer OTP codes, and authenticate collections. |

::: note Administrator Permission Whitelist
A vendor can only assign these capabilities if the marketplace administrator has enabled them in the platform-wide staff settings. For detailed setup instructions, see the [Vendor Staff Guide](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-staff.html).
:::

---

## Best Practices for In-Store Fulfillment

To ensure smooth operations at your retail counter, follow these recommendations:

1. **Pre-Pack Pickup Orders**: When an order enters **Processing** status, pack and label the items in advance so they are ready the moment the customer walks in.
2. **Keep the Pickup Dashboard Open**: Front-counter cashiers should keep `/seller/store-pickup/` open in a browser tab during store hours for fast lookup.
3. **Verify Before Handover**: Always verify the 6-digit OTP code before physically handing bags or boxes across the counter.
4. **Handle Expired Codes Promptly**: If a customer took longer than expected to visit or open their email, click the resend button to generate a fresh code immediately.
5. **Mark Completed Immediately**: Save the order as **Completed** right after successful verification to keep your inventory, payouts, and order logs up to date.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### What if the customer cannot find their verification email?
First, ask the customer to check their **Spam** or **Junk** mail folder for the pickup notification email. Ensure they are checking the exact billing email address displayed on the order record. If the email still has not arrived, click **Send code** again to trigger a fresh OTP.

### Can an order contain products for both home shipping and store pickup?
No. In WooCommerce, shipping methods are selected per order package during checkout. If a buyer chooses **Store Pickup**, all items from that vendor in the order are designated for in-store collection at that vendor's address.

### What address is displayed to the customer for collection?
The system displays your store's physical address configured in your seller profile under **Store Edit** (`/seller/vendor-profile/`), including your street address, city, state, postal code, and contact phone number. Ensure your store profile address is always up to date.

### How does store pickup appear on invoices and packing slips?
The shipping method on the customer invoice and vendor order receipt will clearly state **Store Pickup**, alongside the vendor's physical shop address. You can print invoices directly from the order page by clicking **Print Invoice**.

## How to Access the Vendor Invoice

Follow these simple steps to view and generate an invoice for any order:

1. Log in to your **Vendor Account**.
2. From the left navigation menu, navigate to **Sales > Order History** (`/seller/vendor-orders/`).
3. Locate the order you want to review and click the **Order ID** link or the **View** button.
4. On the **Order Details** screen (for example, `/seller/vendor-orders/1171/`), look at the top-right header section.
5. Click the **Print Invoice** button.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-order-invoice-actions.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-order-invoice-actions.png" alt="Vendor Order Details Header with Print Invoice Button" /></a>

The invoice view opens automatically in a clean, dedicated browser tab at `/vendor/invoice/{encoded_order_id}`.

::: tip Fast Direct Access
The **Print Invoice** button opens the invoice in a new browser window or tab. This allows you to inspect or print the receipt without losing your place in the seller order management workflow.
:::

## Invoice Sections Explained

The vendor invoice is organized into clear, structured sections designed for both digital viewing and physical paperwork:

### 1. Order & Seller Information

At the top of the invoice, two information cards present seller and order details side by side:

- **Seller Information (Left Column)**:
  - **Shop Name**: Your official store display name (e.g., *Aurora Athletics*).
  - **Seller Contact**: Vendor owner name and business location (e.g., *Portland, US*).
  - **Email**: Vendor contact email address.
  - **Profile Link**: Live clickable link to your public storefront.
- **Order Information (Right Column)**:
  - **Order Date**: The exact date the customer placed the order (e.g., *October 21, 2026*).
  - **Order ID**: The marketplace order reference number (e.g., *#1171*).
  - **Payment Method**: The checkout payment option selected by the customer (e.g., *Cash on delivery*, *Credit Card*, *PayPal*).
  - **Shipping Method**: The chosen delivery service or pickup location (e.g., *Store Pickup: Aurora Athletics*).

---

### 2. Buyer Details

This section gives vendors the contact details required for order fulfillment and customer communication:

- **Customer Name**: Full name of the customer who placed the order.
- **Customer Email**: Direct email address for order notifications.
- **Telephone**: Contact phone number, formatted as a clickable telephone link for quick mobile communication.

---

### 3. Product Breakdown Table

The itemized product table displays every item belonging to the seller within that order:

- **Product**: Shows a high-quality product image thumbnail, the product title, selected variation options (such as size or color), and the **Sold By** seller link.
- **Quantity**: The number of units purchased by the customer.
- **Unit Price**: The standard unit price per item.
- **Total**: The line item subtotal (Quantity × Unit Price).

---

### 4. Financial Calculations & Net Earnings

Below the items table, the invoice shows an accurate summary of order financials:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-invoice-view-full.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-invoice-view-full.png" alt="Itemized Table and Financial Summary on Vendor Invoice" /></a>

The financial summary includes:

- **SubTotal**: Combined total price of all items sold by the vendor.
- **Discount** *(if applicable)*: Any coupon or promotional discount deducted from the items.
- **Shipping** *(if applicable)*: Delivery fee collected for the vendor's items.
- **Commission**: The platform administrator commission deducted from the seller's earnings, clearly shown with a minus sign (e.g., `- $4.08`).
- **Tax** *(if applicable)*: Any applicable sales tax or VAT collected.
- **Refunded** *(if applicable)*: Any refunded amount, with the original subtotal struck through for auditing clarity.
- **Total**: The **Net Vendor Earning** for the order. This is the exact amount payable to the vendor after commission deductions.

$$\text{Net Vendor Total} = \text{SubTotal} + \text{Shipping} + \text{Tax} - \text{Admin Commission} - \text{Refunds}$$

---

### 5. Billing and Shipping Addresses

At the bottom of the invoice, the customer's delivery details are displayed in a clean, two-column table:

- **Billing Address**: The customer's official billing address on file with their payment provider.
- **Shipping Address**: The delivery destination for physical package dispatch.

---

## How to Print or Save as PDF

The invoice view includes a built-in print action button:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-invoice-header-action.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-invoice-header-action.png" alt="Print Invoice Button on Vendor Invoice View" /></a>

### Printing a Paper Copy

1. In the top-right corner of the invoice page, click the **Print** icon button.
2. Your browser's print dialog opens immediately.
3. Select your local printer, choose the paper size (A4 or Letter), and click **Print**.

### Saving as a Digital PDF

1. Click the **Print** icon button.
2. In the printer destination dropdown, select **Save as PDF** (or **Microsoft Print to PDF**).
3. Choose your desired orientation (Portrait is recommended).
4. Click **Save** and select a folder on your computer to store the invoice file.

::: info Clean Print Styling
The invoice is automatically styled for print. Browser headers, footers, website menus, and button icons are hidden on printed pages to ensure a clean, corporate invoice.
:::

---

## Custom Vendor Invoice Upload

In addition to viewing and printing the system-generated invoice, vendors can upload their own external tax invoices or accounting documents (such as QuickBooks, Xero, or government tax e-invoices).

### Where to Find Invoice Upload

On the single order details page (`/seller/vendor-orders/{order_id}/`), locate the **Vendor Invoices** box positioned directly below the order status banner:

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-invoice-upload-box.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-invoice-upload-box.png" alt="Vendor Invoices Custom Upload Meta Box" /></a>

### How to Upload a Custom Invoice

1. In the **Invoice Name** field, type a clear title for your document (for example, `VAT-Tax-Invoice-1171`).
2. Click the **Choose File** button and select your invoice file from your device (supported formats: PDF, PNG, JPG, DOCX).
3. Click the **Save** button.
4. Once saved, the document appears in the uploaded invoices table with the following options:
   - **Download Invoice**: Download the saved file back to your device.
   - **View Invoice**: Open the file in a new browser tab for verification.
   - **Delete Invoice**: Remove an outdated or incorrect invoice file.

::: tip Automatic Customer Delivery
If the marketplace administrator has enabled **Attach in mail** in [Configuration – Vendor Invoice](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/configuration-vendor-invoice.html), your uploaded custom invoice is automatically attached to the order notification email sent to the customer.
:::

# Vendor Transaction Management

The **Vendor Transaction Management** section provides marketplace sellers with an intuitive financial center to track order earnings, view marketplace commissions, monitor payout statuses, configure payment withdrawal methods, and submit withdrawal requests directly from the dedicated seller portal.

---

## Access Transactions & Earnings

Vendors can access their financial records at any time:
1. Log in to the **Seller Dashboard**.
2. From the left navigation menu, expand **Sales** and select **Transactions & Earnings** (`/seller/vendor-transactions/`).
3. You can click the **Proceed to Withdraw** button in the top header to navigate directly to the withdrawal management section.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-transactions-dashboard.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-transactions-dashboard.png" alt="Vendor Transactions and Earnings Dashboard" /></a>

::: tip Classic My Account Layout
**Using the traditional WooCommerce My Account interface?**  
If your store operates on the classic tabbed portal (**My Account → Transactions**) instead of the dedicated seller dashboard, refer to the [Classic Transaction Management](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/classic-transaction-management.html) guide.
:::

---

## Financial Overview Cards

At the top of the dashboard, five real-time summary cards provide a quick snapshot of the vendor's financial standing:

| Metric Card | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Total Earning** | Total gross revenue accumulated from all completed marketplace orders. |
| **Total Withdraw** | Cumulative payout amount successfully transferred to the vendor to date. |
| **Total Pending Withdraw** | Current balance available for withdrawal or currently awaiting administrator approval. |
| **Total Refunded** | Total deductions resulting from cancelled orders or customer refund claims. |
| **Last Withdraw** | Exact payout amount processed in the seller's most recent withdrawal. |

---

## Searching and Sorting Transactions

Vendors can filter their transaction records to locate specific payout entries or audit monthly sales:

- **Search Bar**: Enter a transaction ID, order number, or customer name to find matching entries immediately.
- **Sort By Dropdown**: Organize transactions by price or timestamp:
  - **Newest First** *(Default)*: Lists recent transactions at the top.
  - **Price - Low to high**: Displays entries starting from lowest amounts (including fee deductions) to highest.
  - **Price - High to low**: Displays highest-earning transactions first.

---

## Transaction History Table

The transactions table displays all financial credits and debits logged for the seller's store:

| Column | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Transaction ID** | Unique reference number assigned to each transaction. |
| **Transaction Date** | The date and time the financial transaction was recorded. |
| **Customer Name** | Name of the buyer who placed the order (or `Guest` for system fee adjustments). |
| **Total Amount** | Net amount credited to your balance or fee deducted for processing. |
| **Action** | Click **View** to open the itemized breakdown of the transaction. |

::: note Transaction ID Notation
The system assigns specific prefixes to help vendors easily identify entry types:
- **Order Earnings**: Prefixed with `wc_tr-` for revenues earned from customer orders.
- **Withdrawal Charges**: Prefixed with `wd-charge-` for processing or gateway fee deductions applied to a payout.
:::

---

## Itemized Transaction Details

Clicking **View** on any transaction opens a detailed breakdown page with complete line items and commission calculations.

### 1. Order Earnings Transaction
When viewing an order transaction, sellers can verify:
- **Information Panel**: Transaction Date, Net Amount credited, Transaction Type (`Manual`/system), and Disbursement Method.
- **Order Items Breakdown Table**:
  - **Order Id**: Linked marketplace order number (e.g., `#1091`).
  - **Product Name**: Purchased catalog items.
  - **Quantity**: Units sold.
  - **Total Price**: Gross order item price.
  - **Commission**: Marketplace administrator commission deducted according to store commission rules.
  - **Discount**: Applied promotional discounts, if any.
  - **Subtotal**: Final net earnings credited to the seller's balance.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-transaction-order-breakdown.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-transaction-order-breakdown.png" alt="Vendor Order Transaction Detail Breakdown" /></a>

### 2. Withdrawal Fee Transaction
When an administrator charges a processing or transfer fee for a withdrawal, a dedicated debit transaction is recorded with a negative amount (e.g., `-$6.35`). This gives vendors complete transparency into bank transfer or payment gateway processing fees.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-transaction-fee-breakdown.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-transaction-fee-breakdown.png" alt="Vendor Withdrawal Fee Transaction Detail" /></a>

---

## Withdrawal Management

Vendors can access withdrawal settings either by clicking **Proceed to Withdraw** from the transactions dashboard or visiting `/seller/vendor-withdrawal/`.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-withdrawal-dashboard.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-withdrawal-dashboard.png" alt="Vendor Withdrawal Management Dashboard" /></a>

### Adding Withdrawal Payment Methods
Before requesting payouts, vendors must configure at least one active withdrawal method from the **Add Withdrawal Method** dropdown:

1. **Bank Transfer**:
   - Opens the **Add Bank Details** dialog.
   - Enter Account Holder Name, Account Number, Bank Name, Bank Address, IFSC Code, SWIFT Code, Bank IBAN, and Routing Number.
   - Click **Submit** to store the banking credentials securely.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-withdrawal-bank-modal.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-withdrawal-bank-modal.png" alt="Add Bank Details Modal" /></a>

2. **UPI**:
   - Opens the **Add UPI Method** dialog.
   - Enter your valid UPI ID (Virtual Payment Address).
   - Click **Submit** to save.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-withdrawal-upi-modal.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-withdrawal-upi-modal.png" alt="Add UPI Method Modal" /></a>

3. **PayPal**:
   - Enter your PayPal registered email address to receive direct payouts.

### Managing Saved Payment Methods
For every configured payment method, vendors can:
- **Make Default**: Designates the payment method as the primary destination for automatic payouts.
- **Edit** *(Pencil Icon)*: Modify account information or email addresses.
- **Delete**: Remove obsolete withdrawal channels.

---

## Tracking Recent Withdrawals

The **Recent Withdrawals** table logs all submitted payout requests and their lifecycle statuses:

| Column | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Withdrawal ID** | Unique system request identifier. |
| **Amount** | Total payout amount requested by the vendor. |
| **Charges** | Processing or gateway fees applied to the withdrawal transfer. |
| **Method** | Payment channel selected (e.g., PayPal, Bank Transfer, UPI). |
| **Status** | Current processing stage: <br>• <span style="color:#059669;font-weight:600;">Paid</span> – Successfully disbursed by admin. <br>• <span style="color:#d97706;font-weight:600;">Pending</span> – Awaiting administrator review and release. |
| **Created At** | Date and time the withdrawal request was submitted. |

---

## Requesting a New Withdrawal

To request a payout of available order earnings:

1. On the **Withdrawals** page, click the **Request Withdrawals** button.
2. The system redirects to the **Make Withdrawal Requests** view (`/seller/vendor-withdrawal/#/requests`).
3. **Select Orders**: Check the boxes next to completed orders you wish to withdraw funds for (or use the master checkbox to select all).
4. Click **Calculate Total** to calculate the aggregate withdrawal amount and view any applicable transaction charges.
5. Click **Make Withdrawal Requests** to confirm and transmit the payout request to the marketplace administrator.
6. Once submitted, return to **Recent Withdrawals** to monitor status updates as the administrator processes your payment.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-withdrawal-requests-table.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-withdrawal-requests-table.png" alt="Make Withdrawal Requests Screen" /></a>

```
Completed Orders
       │
       ▼
Transactions & Earnings List  ──►  Review Order Earnings & Commissions
       │
       ▼ (Proceed to Withdraw)
Withdrawal Dashboard  ──────────►  Configure Payment Method (Bank / UPI / PayPal)
       │
       ▼ (Request Withdrawals)
Select Eligible Orders  ────────►  Calculate Total & Submit Request
       │
       ▼
Admin Approval & Payout  ───────►  Status Updates to "Paid" in Recent Withdrawals
```

# Vendor Account Health

In **WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace**, **Account Health** provides sellers with an immediate, transparent view of their standing and operational quality across the marketplace. Maintaining high account health builds customer confidence, increases sales conversion, and helps sellers maintain good standing with marketplace administrators.

The Account Health report evaluates real store performance using three core criteria:
1. **Order Cancellation Rate** (preventing cancelled orders after payment)
2. **Customer Feedback** (average rating across store reviews)
3. **Flags Raised** (complaints or policy reports submitted against your shop or products)

In addition to the overall health score, sellers can review key operational insights—including **Refund Rates**, **Product Reviews**, and **Fulfillment Completion Times**—and experiment with an interactive **Live Calculator** to simulate how operational improvements will boost their overall score.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-account-health-dashboard.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-account-health-dashboard.png" alt="Vendor Account Health Dashboard Overview in WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace" /></a>

---

## Navigating to Account Health

Vendors can access their Account Health console using two quick methods from the seller workspace:

1. **Via Seller Navigation Sidebar:**
   - Log in to your registered **Seller Account**.
   - In the left sidebar navigation, expand the **Performance** section.
   - Click **Account Health** to open the dedicated console.
2. **Via Seller Dashboard Stat Card:**
   - Open your main **Seller Dashboard** (`/seller/`).
   - Locate the **Account Health** KPI card among your operational metrics.
   - Click the card to view the complete breakdown and report.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-account-health-stat-card.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-account-health-stat-card.png" alt="Vendor Dashboard Account Health KPI Stat Card" /></a>

| Access Method | Location / Path | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Direct URL** | `/seller/seller-account-health/` | Opens the full Account Health report, scored metrics, and operational insights. |
| **Calculation Guide** | `/seller/seller-account-health/?wkmp_view=guide` | Detailed breakdown of scoring formulas, rules, tips, and the interactive live calculator. |
| **Dashboard Stat Card** | `/seller/` | High-level summary displaying your health band, score out of 100, and a 12-month trend sparkline. |

::: tip Instant Real-Time Updates
Your Account Health report is calculated on-demand from live marketplace data every time you visit the page. New orders, completed transactions, customer reviews, or flag reports are reflected immediately without manual recalculation.
:::

---

## Overall Health Score & Performance Bands

At the top of the Account Health screen, the **Overall Health** card highlights your current status, numerical score, and operational band:

- **Health Score (0–100):** A weighted performance score calculated from your store's cancellation rate, customer review ratings, and flags.
- **Health Band Indicator:** A multi-colored status gauge showing where your score falls along the marketplace performance spectrum.
- **Current Standing Message:** A clear explanation of your current status (for example: *"Your account is in good standing. Keep it up."*).

### Performance Band Thresholds

| Performance Band | Score Range | Status Meaning & Recommended Action |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Healthy** | **80 – 100** | **Good Standing:** Your business operations meet all marketplace standards. Keep inventory updated and fulfill orders quickly to maintain this level. |
| **At Risk** | **50 – 79** | **Needs Improvement:** Your score has slipped due to cancelled orders, lower customer ratings, or reported flags. Address customer complaints and review stock levels promptly. |
| **Unhealthy** | **0 – 49** | **Action Required:** Your store operations are below marketplace expectations. Investigate order bottlenecks, resolve pending issues with buyers, and update product descriptions. |
| **Not Enough Data Yet** | **— / 100** | **Pending Activity:** Your score will automatically appear once your store receives at least 1 paid order or 1 approved customer review during the selected period. |

---

## Core Scored Metrics

Your overall health score is composed of **three primary operational metrics**. Each metric earns between 0 and 100 points based on predefined marketplace targets and fail points:

### 1. Order Cancellation Rate (Base Weight: 40%)

The **Order Cancellation Rate** tracks the share of product units in paid orders that were cancelled.

- **Standard Timeframe:** Last 30 days (grouped by the date the order was placed).
- **Target (100 Points):** Below **2.5%**.
- **Fail Point (0 Points):** **10.0%** or higher.
- **Fair Accounting Rule:** Only **paid orders** count toward cancellations. If a customer cancels an order before completing payment, or if an unpaid checkout expires, it is **never** held against you.
- **Unit-Level Tracking:** If an order contains 4 units and 1 unit is cancelled, the calculation accurately reflects 1 of 4 units cancelled rather than marking the entire order as cancelled.

### 2. Customer Feedback (Base Weight: 35%)

The **Customer Feedback** metric measures overall store satisfaction from approved reviews submitted by buyers.

- **Standard Timeframe:** Last 90 days.
- **Target (100 Points):** **4.0 stars** or higher.
- **Fail Point (0 Points):** **2.0 stars** or lower.
- **Balanced Dimensional Average:** Each review score is calculated as the average of the customer's ratings across three distinct dimensions: **Price**, **Value**, and **Quality**.
- **Quick Action:** Click the **View reviews** link on the card to jump directly to your [Seller Reviews](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-seller-review.html) dashboard.

### 3. Flags Raised (Base Weight: 25%)

The **Flags** metric counts buyer reports submitted against your shop profile or individual product listings.

- **Standard Timeframe:** Last 90 days.
- **Target (100 Points):** **0 flags** (no reports).
- **Fail Point (0 Points):** **10 flags** (red flag limit) or more.
- **Itemized Breakdown:** The metric card clearly displays how many flags were submitted against your **store** versus your **products** (e.g., *0 on your store · 1 on your products*).
- **Goal:** The fewer flags raised, the higher your score.

---

## Dynamic Weight Sharing & Scoring Rules

The marketplace uses an intelligent **proportional weight-sharing model** so sellers are never unfairly penalized when specific data is not yet available:

<div class="wkmp-decision-grid">
  <div class="wkmp-outcome-box wkmp-outcome-box--approved">
    <div class="wkmp-outcome-box__header">
      <span class="wkmp-outcome-box__badge wkmp-outcome-box__badge--approved">Standard Scoring</span>
      <span class="wkmp-outcome-box__scope">With Reviews</span>
    </div>
    <div class="wkmp-outcome-box__title wkmp-outcome-box__title--approved">Full 3-Metric Distribution</div>
    <ul class="wkmp-outcome-box__points">
      <li class="wkmp-outcome-box__point"><strong>Order Cancellation Rate:</strong> 40% base weight</li>
      <li class="wkmp-outcome-box__point"><strong>Customer Feedback:</strong> 35% base weight</li>
      <li class="wkmp-outcome-box__point"><strong>Store & Product Flags:</strong> 25% base weight</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="wkmp-outcome-box" style="background: #f0f9ff; border: 1px solid #bae6fd;">
    <div class="wkmp-outcome-box__header">
      <span class="wkmp-outcome-box__badge" style="background: #0284c7; color: #ffffff;">Adjusted Scoring</span>
      <span class="wkmp-outcome-box__scope">No Reviews Yet</span>
    </div>
    <div class="wkmp-outcome-box__title" style="color: #0369a1;">Proportional Redistribution</div>
    <ul class="wkmp-outcome-box__points">
      <li class="wkmp-outcome-box__point"><strong>Customer Feedback:</strong> Omitted without penalty</li>
      <li class="wkmp-outcome-box__point"><strong>Order Cancellation Rate:</strong> Automatically shares weight (~62%)</li>
      <li class="wkmp-outcome-box__point"><strong>Store & Product Flags:</strong> Automatically shares weight (~38%)</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>

### How Proportional Redistribution Works

1. **Metric Without Data is Omitted:** If your store has no customer reviews in the active 90-day window, the Customer Feedback metric is omitted from the score denominator.
2. **Remaining Metrics Share the Weight:** The remaining active metrics share the missing weight in proportion to their base values:
   - **Order Cancellation Rate:** $(40 \div 65) \times 100 \approx \mathbf{62\%}$ of your score.
   - **Flags Raised:** $(25 \div 65) \times 100 \approx \mathbf{38\%}$ of your score.
3. **Minimum Activity Threshold:** Flags alone do not reflect how a seller conducts business. A score requires active selling data (at least **1 paid order** or **1 approved review**). If neither exists, the status displays **Not enough data yet** (`— / 100`).

### Scoring Criteria Reference Table

| Metric Name | Evaluation Window | Target (Full 100 Pts) | Fail Point (0 Pts) | Base Weight | Active Without Reviews |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Order Cancellation Rate** | Last 30 days | $2.5\%$ or less | $10.0\%$ or more | **40%** | **62%** |
| **Customer Feedback** | Last 90 days | $4.0$ or higher | $2.0$ or lower | **35%** | *Excluded* |
| **Flags on Store & Products** | Last 90 days | $0$ flags | $10$ flags or more | **25%** | **38%** |

::: info Points Scale Linearly
Between the target (100 points) and the fail point (0 points), your score decreases evenly in a straight line. For example, if your cancellation rate is halfway between 2.5% and 10.0%, you receive 50 points for that metric.
:::

---

## Additional Operational Insights

Below the core score cards, the **More insights** section provides additional diagnostic metrics. These figures help you optimize shop operations, but **they are not part of your numerical health score**:

### 1. Refund Rate
- **Timeframe:** Last 30 days (by order date).
- **What It Measures:** The percentage of units in paid orders that were refunded, alongside the total refunded dollar amount (for example: *0% · 0 of 3 units refunded · $0.00*).
- **Seller Benefit:** Helps you identify product quality issues, shipping damage, or inaccurate product descriptions before they result in buyer disputes.

### 2. Product Reviews
- **Timeframe:** Last 90 days.
- **What It Measures:** The average star rating (1 to 5 stars) across all approved customer reviews left specifically on your product listings.
- **Action Link:** Click **View product reviews** to inspect buyer comments on individual items in your [Product Reviews](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/woocommerce-marketplace/documentation/vendor-reviews.html) manager.

### 3. Paid → Completed (Fulfillment Time)
- **Timeframe:** Last 30 days (by order date).
- **What It Measures:** The average time taken from when the buyer paid until your order was marked **Completed**.
- **Fairness in Multi-Seller Orders:** Orders containing items from multiple independent vendors are excluded from this metric because overall order completion depends on the slowest seller. Only orders containing your products exclusively are measured.

---

## Filtering Performance by Time Periods ("Choose period")

By default, Account Health uses standard rolling windows (30 days for orders and fulfillment; 90 days for reviews and flags). Sellers can adjust this to evaluate performance over specific seasonal campaigns, promotional periods, or quarters.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-account-health-filter-drawer.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-account-health-filter-drawer.png" alt="Account Health Period Filter Drawer with Presets and Date Range" /></a>

### How to Use the Filter Drawer

1. Click the **Choose period** button in the page header.
2. The **Choose period** filter panel slides in from the right edge of the screen.
3. Select either a **Quick Date Preset** or define a **Custom Date Range**:
   - **Quick Presets:**
     - Today
     - Yesterday
     - This Week
     - This Month
     - Last Month
     - Last 3 Months
     - Last 6 Months
     - This Year
   - **Custom Range:** Select a **From date** and a **To date** (supports spans up to 12 months; leaving the *To date* blank automatically defaults to today).
4. Click the blue **Apply** button to update your report.

::: tip Automatic Flag Limit Scaling
When you select a custom period, every metric evaluates data across that chosen timeframe, and the **Red Flag Limit** scales proportionally. For example, in a 1-month custom period, the flag limit adjusts from 10 flags down to approximately 4 flags, maintaining equal fairness across different timeframe lengths.
:::

---

## Account Health Calculation Guide & Live Calculator

To understand the exact mechanics behind your score, click the **"How is this calculated?"** link in the top header. This opens the dedicated **Health Calculation Guide** (`?wkmp_view=guide`).

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-account-health-guide-calculator.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-account-health-guide-calculator.png" alt="Account Health Calculation Guide and Interactive Live Calculator" /></a>

### Practical Seller Recommendations

The guide highlights five key operational habits to protect and improve your score:

1. **Keep stock and prices updated:** Ensure product inventory counts are accurate so you never have to cancel a paid order due to stockouts.
2. **Pack and dispatch promptly:** Package products securely and mark orders as completed as soon as they are handed over to shipping carriers.
3. **Accurate product listings:** Provide clear photos, detailed specifications, and truthful descriptions so buyers receive exactly what they expect.
4. **Fast customer support:** Reply quickly to buyer queries and resolve complaints before they turn into store flags or negative reviews.
5. **Clear store policies:** Maintain explicit shipping and return policies on your vendor profile so customers know what to expect.

### Using the Interactive Live Calculator

At the bottom of the calculation guide, vendors can use an **interactive simulation tool**:

- **Pre-filled with your current figures:** When opened, the calculator loads your real live statistics.
- **Customer Reviews Toggle:** Switch between **With reviews** and **No reviews** to see how review presence affects metric weights.
- **Interactive Sliders:**
  - **Flags raised:** Adjust from 0 to 20 flags to see how buyer reports impact your standing.
  - **Average rating:** Move the rating slider between 1.0 and 5.0 stars.
  - **Order cancellation rate:** Test cancellation percentages from 0% up to 20%.
- **Instant Result:** The calculator instantly shows the simulated **Health Score (0–100)** and **Health Band** (Healthy, At Risk, or Unhealthy).
- **Safe Testing:** Nothing in the calculator is saved or modifies your live store data. It is purely an exploratory tool for sellers.

# Seller Review

In **WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace**, **Seller Reviews** allow vendors to track customer feedback submitted specifically for their store profile. While product reviews focus on individual catalog items, seller reviews reflect overall store performance—including customer service, order fulfillment speed, packaging care, and communication.

Monitoring your store reviews helps you understand buyer satisfaction, build a trusted brand reputation, and maintain a high rating in your [Vendor Account Health](https://wpdoc.webkul.com/documentation/vendor-account-health.html) score.

<a class="doc-image-link" href="./assets/vendor-seller-reviews-list.png"><img src="./assets/vendor-seller-reviews-list.png" alt="Vendor Seller Reviews Dashboard in WooCommerce Multi-Vendor Marketplace" /></a>

---

## Accessing Seller Reviews

Vendors can access their Seller Reviews console directly from the vendor dashboard:

1. Log in to your **Seller Account**.
2. In the left navigation menu, locate the **Performance** group.
3. Click **Seller Reviews** to open the dedicated reviews console.

Alternatively, you can open the **Account Health** page (`/seller/seller-account-health/`) and click the **View reviews** link on the Customer Feedback KPI card.

| **Seller Navigation Menu** | `Performance` &rarr; `Seller Reviews` | View the complete list of store-level reviews and ratings. |
| **Direct URL** | `/seller/seller-reviews/` | Direct access to the seller reviews console. |
| **Account Health Shortcut** | `/seller/seller-account-health/` | Click **View reviews** to jump directly to store feedback. |

::: tip Mobile Navigation
On smartphones and small tablets, tap the **Open menu** button in the top bar to expand the sidebar navigation, open **Performance**, and select **Seller Reviews**.

| **Customer / Email** | &bull; Customer Full Name<br>&bull; Buyer Avatar / Initials<br>&bull; Registered Email Address | Identifies the customer who submitted the review so you can track order history and buyer relationships. |

| **Title / Rating / Description** | &bull; Overall Average Rating (e.g., *Rated 5 out of 5*)<br>&bull; 3-Pillar Breakdown (**Price**, **Value**, and **Quality**)<br>&bull; Review Headline / Title<br>&bull; Customer Comment Description | Provides full qualitative and quantitative feedback on your store performance. |
